For the fifth day: the first and last *paryāyas* consist of the verses beginning with *trikadrukeṣu*, which are always accompanied by their respective *vatsas*. For the first of the *atīṣaṅga* chants, one uses the verses beginning with *indrāyāhi* and *yadindra citram*. For the middle *paryāya* of the *mahānāmnīs*, one uses the verses beginning with *vidā maghavan*. This is the *pṛṣṭha-stotra* of the Hotṛ; everything else is the same as on the fifth day.

For the sixth day: "indrāyendave" is the Gāyatra; the *aiśovṛdhīya*, *krauñca*, *vājadāvya*, *yadārḍhacyuta*, and *raivatā* [stotras follow]. "mṛjyamānaḥ" is the *svāra*; the *aukṣṇorandhra* and *aiḍa-aukṣṇorandhra* are for two triplets (*tṛca*). The *kaulmalabarhiṣa*, *vājajit*, and *varuṇasāman* are the *sāmatṛcas*. The *goṣṭha* is for three verses. "etamu tyam" is the final *vāmadevya* like that of the *ihavat*. "revatīr naḥ" is the *vāravantīya*, the *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ. Or else:

The first and last *paryāya*s of the Dārḍhacyuta are "revām̐ idrevā. The middle *paryāya* of the Vāravantīya is "revatīrṇa. Alternatively, the first and last *paryāya*s of the Dārḍhacyuta are "revatīrṇa," and the middle *paryāya* of the Vāravantīya is in that same *ṛc*-verse triplet. The rest is the same as with the sixth [day].
He states the nature of the six-day periods consisting of the *prāṅkya* and *pṛṣṭha* sequences for the sixteenth and seventeenth days:
"Now, therefore, follow the two six-day periods consisting of the *prāṅkya* and *pṛṣṭha*."

The Fourth Chapter: The Alternatives for the *Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*. That which deserves a mark (*aṅka*) or a position is called *aṅkyam*. Because the *pṛṣṭha* chants that are directly perceived (*pratyakṣa*) are displaced slightly from their positions on both sides, they are termed *prāṅkya*. Those two [six-day periods] are thus described as having *pṛṣṭha* chants that are *prāṅkya*. He states the designation for both based on the difference in their characteristics:
"the one with indirect *prāṅkya-pṛṣṭhas*, and the one with direct *prāṅkya-pṛṣṭhas*" (Sūtra 4).
Thus [ends the fourth section].
He states the arrangement:

"The ritual procedure for those two is as follows: the first turn belongs to the indirect (parokṣa) [six-day period], while the latter two belong to the direct (pratyakṣa). That six-day period has its front and back turned toward the indirect. (5)

Thus it is clear. For the first day, the first *paryāya* of the *kaṇvarathantara* is "abhi tvā śūra. In that same triplet (*tṛca*), the two following [stotras] are for the *rathantara*. This constitutes the *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ. Everything else is the same as on the first day.

For the second day: the first *paryāya* is "tvām id dhi" from the *kaṇva-bṛhat*, belonging either to the *bṛhannidhana* or the *vārkajaṃbha* [sāman]. The two subsequent [paryāyas] are [performed] on that same *ṛc* with the *bṛhat* [sāman]. This is the *pṛṣṭha-stotra* of the Hotṛ. Everything else is the same as on the second day.

Regarding the third day: the first *paryāya* belongs either to the *hrasvā-bṛhat* [stoma] with the *upaśa* "yad dyāvaḥ," or to the *antarikṣa*, or to the *mahāvaiṣṭambha*. On that same triplet (*ṛca*), the two following [verses] belong to the *vairūpa*. This is the *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ. In the case of the *antarikṣa* [pakṣa], at the midday pressing, *añjovairūpa* takes the place of the *antarikṣa*. In the case of the *mahāvaiṣṭambha* [pakṣa], "vayaṃ gha tvā" with the *abhinidhana* [sāman] of the Kaṇvas is the *brahman*s [pṛṣṭha]. This is the *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ. Everything else is like the third day.

For the fourth day: "Drink the Soma"—this is the first *paryāya* of the *ṛṣabha* of Vairāja, belonging either to Sahoda Dīrghatamasa or to Vasiṣṭha Vairāja; the two following [verses] are of the *mahāvairāja*. These constitute the *pṛṣṭha* stotra of the Hotṛ. The rest is the same as on the fourth day.

For the fifth day: "In the Trikadrukas"—this is the first *paryāya* for those [stotras] whose calves are permanently tied; "Come, O Indra"—in these verses beginning with "O Indra, that which is wonderful," or for the first of the *atīṣaṅga* stotras; "May we find, O Bountiful One"—in these verses, the two following [verses] belong to the *mahānāmnīs*. Thus is the *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ. The rest is the same as on the fifth day.

Regarding the sixth day: the *vāravantīya* chant, beginning with "revatīr naḥ," is the *pṛṣṭha* stotra of the Hotṛ priest. Alternatively, the first *paryāya* belongs to the *dārḍhacyuta* [chant] beginning with "revām̐ idra"; the two following [paryāyas] belong to the *vāravantīya* beginning with "revatīr naḥ. Or else, the first *paryāya* belongs to the *dārḍhacyuta* beginning with "revatīr naḥ," while the two following [paryāyas] belong to the *vāravantīya* on that same triplet (*tṛca*). Everything else is like the sixth day of the *pratyakṣāparkya-pṛṣṭha* six-day rite (*ṣaḍaha*). 5.5.105.1–2.
He states the second [classification]:

"The first variant belongs to perception (*pratyakṣa*); the latter two belong to indirect knowledge (*parokṣa*). That six-day rite (*ṣaḍaha*) has perception at its beginning and at its end. (6) Thus [ends section] 6.
The Fourth Chapter: Alternative Forms of the Pṛṣṭhya-Ṣaḍaha [The Parokṣopāṅkyapṛṣṭha and the Pratyakṣopāṅkyapṛṣṭha].
Now, therefore, follow the two Upāṅkyapṛṣṭha Ṣaḍahas: the Parokṣopāṅkyapṛṣṭha and the Pratyakṣopāṅkyapṛṣṭha.

[He states the arrangement:]—The ritual procedure for those two is as follows: for the *pratyakṣa* [sacrifice], there are the first two turns; for the *parokṣa*, the last one. That is the six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) consisting of the *parokṣa*, the *upāṃśu*, and the *pṛṣṭha*. 8.
[He states the second:
"The first two modes belong to the indirect (*parokṣa*), while the last belongs to the direct (*pratyakṣa*); that six-day rite (*ṣaḍaha*) has the mark of the direct as its back. (9)

Thus it is clearly stated. Regarding the first day: the first two *paryāyas* consist of the *rathantara* [sāman] with the verse "abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ. The last [paryāya] of that same *rathantara* is performed on that very same triplet (*ṛca*). This constitutes the *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ. The rest is the same as on the first day.

Regarding the second day: for the first two rounds, one uses the *bṛhannidhana* [sāman] on the *tvām id dhi* verse of either the *arkajambha* or the *kaṇvabṛhat* [sāmans]; the last [round] uses the *bṛhat* [sāman] on that same triplet. This is the *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ; everything else is the same as on the second day.

On the third day: *yad dyāvaḥ* [is the stotra] with the *hrasvā-bṛhat* as the *upaśa*; the first two *paryāyas* belong either to the *antarikṣa* or the *mahāvaiṣṭambha*. The last [verse] belongs to the *vairūpa*. This is the *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ. If the *antarikṣa* [view] is adopted, at midday, in the place of the *antarikṣa*, there is the *añjovairūpa*. If the *mahāvaiṣṭambha* view is adopted, *vayaṃ gha tvā* is the *abhinidhana* of the Kaṇva-Brahman. The rest is the same as on the third day.

For the fourth day: "Drink the Soma"—this is the *ṛṣabha* of Vairāja, belonging either to Sahoda Dīrghatamas or to Vasiṣṭha; the first two *paryāyas* belong to Vasiṣṭha’s Vairāja, and the last belongs to the Mahāvairāja. This is the *pṛṣṭha-stotra* of the Hotṛ. Everything else is the same as on the fourth day.

For the fifth day: the first two *paryāyas* consist of the *trikadruka* hymns, which are always accompanied by their respective *vatsas*. For the *atiṣaṅga* hymns, one may use either the verses beginning with "indrāyāhi" and "yadindra citramā" as the first, or the verses beginning with "vidā maghavan" as the last for the *mahānāmnī* hymns. This is the *pṛṣṭha* stotra of the Hotṛ; everything else is the same as on the fifth day.

For the sixth day: the *vāravantīya* chant, beginning with "revatīr naḥ," is the *pṛṣṭha* stotra of the Hotṛ. Alternatively, the first two *paryāyas* belong to the *dārḍhacyuta* chant, "revām indra," while the last belongs to the *vāravantīya*. Or else, the first two *paryāyas* belong to the *dārḍhacyuta* chant, and the last belongs to the *vāravantīya* on that same triplet (*tṛca*). Everything else is as in the sixth day of the *parokṣapraṅkya* six-day rite (*ṣaḍaha*).

If it is argued that in the two subsequent sections there is the fault of "transposition" (*saṃcāra-doṣa*) because the *dārḍhacyuta* chant is performed for both the *mādhyaṃdinapavamāna* and the *hotṛ-pṛṣṭha*, we say: not so. There is no fault because it is prescribed by the author of the *Nidāna*. Just as in the case of the *viśvajit* sacrifices such as the *āptoryāma*, although the *kaṇvarathantara* is prescribed in the middle of the *rathantara*—even though the two *stotrīyā* verses were mentioned first—the author of the *Nidāna* does not accept the transposition as a fault.

Or, just as in the case of the *anurūpa-agniṣṭoma-sāman* on the sixth day of the *dvādaśāha*, although there is an injunction for the *vāravantīya* to be the *hotṛ-pṛṣṭha* and the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*, the author of the *kalpa* did not accept the transference (*saṃcāra*) as a fault; such is the intention of the author of the *nidāna*. Or else:

In the *Jaimini-Kalpasūtra*, because of the injunction— "In the six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) containing the *pṛṣṭhastoma* within the *saṃsadāmayaṇa*, on the sixth day, one should perform either the *āmahīyava* or the *dārḍhacyuta* in the place of the *revatīs*"— here, in the *āpārkya* and other rites, regarding the *mādhyaṃdinapavamāna* and the *hotṛ-pṛṣṭha*, and following the sequence of the *hotṛ-pṛṣṭha* cycles,
[the author] speaks of the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*) based upon the fifteen-fold stomas (*pañcadaśa*) of the ten-night stomas (*daśarātrika*).
Now, there are another ten [chapters]. || 1 ||
Thus [ends the first].
Sixth Chapter – Variations of the Twelve-Day Sacrifice, Section 3, Khanda 15 [The First: The Twelve-Day Sacrifice with the Trivṛt Stoma].
Therein, he first describes the twelve-day sacrifice characterized by the *trivṛt* stoma:
Just as the first day has its specific stoma, so too should this entire ten-night period have its respective stoma. ||2||

Thus: as there is the word *yad*, so there is the word *yathā*; the meaning is "that which has the *stoma*. Likewise, regarding *tathā* here as well, the meaning is that the entire *daśarātra* should be performed with the *trivṛt-stoma*. ||2||
Regarding this, he states the qualified person: "Therefore, one who desires splendor or one who desires Vedic luster should sacrifice with this. (3)

Thus [it is said]. This is clear. Its ritual arrangement (*klṛpti*) is as follows: the insertion (*āvāpa*) and removal (*udvāpa*) of the *stomas* should be performed according to their suitability, as in the case of the *ādityānām ayana*, the *vyūḍha agniṣṭoma*, and the *daśarātra*. The first day is unmodified, like that of the *dvādaśāha*.

For the second day: the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant consists of "Pavasva vācaḥ," "Pavasvendo," and "Pavamānasya te vayam. At the midday pressing, the *sāmatṛcas* are the *gāyatra*, *ukta-aśvasvāra*, and *sauparṇa*. The *sāmatṛcas* are the *aiḍa*, *āyāsya*, *dairghaśravasa*, *triṇidhana*, and *āyāsya*, beginning with "Punānaḥ soma. The final *vāsiṣṭha* hymn, beginning with "Vṛṣā śoṇaḥ," is performed on three verses. In the *ārbhava* pressing, the *gāyatra-hāviṣmata* begins with "Yaste mado vareṇyaḥ" on the first verse.

"Pavasva indram accha" occurs in the two single-verse [hymns] at Śaṅkusujñāna. "Ayaṃ pūṣā" occurs in the first of the Gaurīvita and Krauñca [hymns], because of the statement: "Two [verses] in that very [first]. "Vṛṣā matīnām" occurs in the three [verses] of the Yāma [hymn] as the final one; the others are single-verse [hymns], excluding the final one, because of the statement: "In every case, when the Stoma is possible, the final [hymn] is a triplet. Everything else is like the second day. All is Trivṛt.

For the third day: the *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of the verses "davidyutatyā rucā," "ete asṛgram iṣe pavasva dhārā," and the two single-verse hymns "uccā te" and "gāyatrakṣullakavaiṣṭambha. The three-verse *sāmans* are "abhi some" (the Paurumadga), "abhi some" (the Gautama), and "antarikṣāṇi. The *āṣkāraṇidhana* is used for the *madhyāsyā*. The final [verse] is the "aṅgirasāṃ saṃkrośa" consisting of the three verses beginning with "tisro vācaḥ. In the *ārbhava-pavamāna*, all single-verse hymns are used except for the last one. Everything else is like the third day; everything is in the *trivṛt* stoma.

For the fourth day: the Bahiṣpavamāna chant begins with "pra te pavamāno ajījanat" and "hinvanti sūram. For the Mādhyandina and Ārbhava Pavamānas, the verses consist of single ṛcs, excluding the final ones. Everything else is like the fourth day. All [stomas] are Trivṛt, and there is also the Ṣoḍaśin Sāman.

For the fifth day: *govid viśvavid yāste dhārā* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. *arṣā soma* is the *gāyatra* on one verse; *yaṇvam* on three verses. *soma uṣva* is the *ānūpa* on one verse; on that same [verse] is the *agnestriṇidhana*. *yatsoma citramukthyam* is the *śaiśava*, the final [stotra] of the midday pressing, on three verses. The *santani* *brahmasāman* is based on the *bārhadgira* verses. *asāvyaṃśuḥ* is the *gāyatragauṣūkta*; *abhi dyumnaṃ prāṇā śiśuḥ* is the *cyāvanakrośa*.

"Pavasva vājasātaye"—this is the Gaurīvita; the Ṛṣabha and Śākvara [Sāmans]; "Indur vājī" is the Dāśaspatya; the last [verse] belongs to the Ārbhava [Śastra]. With the exception of the last, they consist of single verses (*ekarcāḥ*). Everything else is like the fifth day. All is threefold (*trivṛt*).

The Sixth Chapter: Variations of the Twelve-Day Rite; the Bahiṣpavamāna of the sixth day. "Jyotir asṛkṣata ete somā abhi priyam"—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna. "Indrāyendavo"—the Gāyatra [Sāman] is performed on a single verse. The Revatī verses are performed on three verses. "Mṛjyamānaḥ"—the Svāra-Aukṣṇorandhra [Sāman] is performed on a single verse. On that same verse, the Goṣṭha [Sāman] is performed. "Etamu tyam"—the Vāmadevya [Sāman], ending with "iha," is performed on three verses for the Mādhyandina Pavamāna. "Parisvāno giriṣṭhāḥ"—the Gāyatra-Tṛtīyavaidannvata [Sāman] is performed. "Sa su taṃ vaḥ sakhāyaḥ"—the Dīrghakārṇaśravasa [Sāman] is performed. "Somāḥ pavante."

Thus [are] the Gaurīvita, Iḍa, and Krauñca [stomas]. With the verses "ayā pavasva" and "pavasva," the final [verse] of the Ārbhava Pavamāna is the Śnauṣṭa. With the exception of the final [verse], the others consist of single verses. Everything else is like the sixth day; everything is threefold (trivṛt).

For the seventh day: *pra kā te dākṣam* is the Bahiṣpavamāna. *vṛṣā pavasva* consists of the Gāyatra, Aiḍa, Sauparṇa, and Rohitakūlīya Sāman-trikas. *punānaḥ soma* consists of the Kaṇvarathantara, Gauṅgava, Sāptamika, and Māyāsya Sāman-trikas. *pro ayāsīt* is the Pravad-Bhārgava, the final [Stotra] of the Mādhyandina, performed on three verses. On the verses of Kāṇva, there is the Saṃtani of Brahmaṇaspati. In the Ārbhava Pavamāna, *yaste madaḥ* consists of the Gāyatra and Agner-arka Sāmans.

"Eṣa sya sakhyāya" and "ti śārkaraplavau"; "purojitī" and "gaurīvitakārtayaśe"; "ye somāsaḥ" is the Jarābodhīya, the final [stotra] of the Ārbhava Pavamāna; with the exception of the final [verse], they consist of single verses (*ekarcāḥ*). Everything else is like the seventh day. All is *trivṛt*.

For the eighth day: these three triplets beginning with *śiśum* are for the new *ṛc*s of the Soma. The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant begins with *ayā pavasva*. The *gāyatravilamba* and *sauparṇa* chants begin with *adhvaryo adribhiḥ*. The triplets of *sāmans*—the *vāmadevya*, *gāyatrapārśva*, and *pauruhanmana*—begin with *abhi soma* and contain two *hiṃkāras*. The *acchidra* chant is used for the middle *stotriya*. The final *mādhyaṃdina* chant is the *udvat* of the Bhārgava family, beginning with *dhartā divaḥ*; all its verses are single *ṛcs* except for the last one. The *gāyatrasvāśira* and *āmarrku* chants begin with *pavasva deva āyuṣi*.

"Abhi dyumnam prāṇā śiśuḥ"—these two [verses] are here [the first and second *aiṣī*]. "Abhī no vājasātamam"—this is the *gaurīvita-padanidhana*, the *śuddha-aśuddhīya*. "Hinvanti"—this is the final *iḍā-nāṃsaṃkṣāra*. With the exception of the final one, they consist of single verses (*ekarccāḥ*). Everything else is like the eighth day. All is *trivṛt*.

For the ninth day: the *tṛca* (three-verse hymn) beginning with "This immortal god has stepped forth" (*akrān eṣa devo amartya*) from the ten-verse hymn; the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant begins with "Of thee, the purifying one, O sage" (*pavamānasya te kava*). For the first [verse], the *gāyatra* and *ādārasṛt* [melodies] are used for the verse beginning "Of the purifying one who strikes down" (*pavamānasya jighnata*). The *pṛṣṭha*, *kaulmalabarhiṣa*, and *devasthāna* [stotras] consist of three-verse hymns of Sāmans beginning with "Around thee" (*parītoṣi*). The *arka* of Dīrghatamas is used for the *adhyāsya*. The "King of Sāmans" (*sāmarāja*), beginning with "Soma has been pressed" (*asāvi soma*), is used for the final [verse] among the three. The *gāyatra* and *aśvasūkta* are used for the verse beginning "Thou, O Soma" (*tvaṃ soma*).

"O member, as a divine one, flow for the feast of the gods," [is the first verse] for Sūparṇa Vaiśvamanasa. "Him, the desirable one... [and] "The Gaurīvita and Saṃkṛti" [are the next two]. "Approach... [is the third], which is the final Ārbhava triplet belonging to Pratīcīna-iḍa Kāśīta. With the exception of the final [verse], these are single-verse stanzas. Everything else is like the ninth day. All [the Śastras] are Trivṛt.

For the tenth day: "They have been let loose, the prize-winners... (RV 9.62.1), "The purifier, the knower of all... (RV 9.86.12), and "The purifying one has brought them forth"—these are three single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*). "These drops have been let loose... (RV 9.63.1) and "Flow on, O Indu, as a bull, pressed... (RV 9.97.1)—these two triple-verse hymns (*tṛcas*) constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant.
Sixth Chapter: Variations of the Twelve-Day Rite (*dvādaśāha*).

The *sāman*-triplets are: the *Gāyatrāmahīyava* and *Ābhīka* on the verses beginning with *uccā ta*; the *Utsedha*, *Gaurīvita*, and *Niṣedha* on the verses beginning with *punānaḥ soma*. The *Yajñāyajñīya* on the verses beginning with *ājāgṛvi* is the final [sāman] of the midday pressing performed on three verses. In the third pressing (*ārbhava*), there is the extraction of the *Sauhaviṣa*; all [verses] except the last one are single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*). However, in the combined midday pressing, the *Maidhātitha* takes the place of the *Gaurīvita*. In the third pressing, the *Gaurīvita* takes the place of the *Śyāvāśva*. Everything else is like the tenth day. The ten rules of commonality (*samānasā daśadharma*) are to be observed. Everything is in the *trivṛt* stoma. 3.
[The fifteen-fold-stoma twelve-day rite is the second.
He speaks of the fifteen-fold-stoma twelve-day rite:
"Just as the second."

Thus [it is said]. The word *stoma* (hymn-form) is understood to carry over. As in the expression "the second day has the *stoma* as its secondary element," the meaning is that whatever *stoma* belongs to the second day, that same *stoma* should be employed for the entire ten-night rite (*daśarātra*). The same principle should be applied to the subsequent days. ||4||
Regarding this, he states the qualified person:
"Therefore, one who desires splendor or one who desires vigor [should perform it]. (5)

Thus it is said; the word *yajeta* (one should sacrifice) is understood to carry over. Regarding that, for the first day: the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is "asya pratnāmanu dyutaṃ daviṣva pavasva" (RV 9.1). Insertions and deletions (*āvāpodvāpa*) should be made according to the requirements of the *stoma*, as in the *ādityānāmayana*, the *chandoma*, and the *daśarātra*. The *gāyatrāśvasomasāmans* are "pra somāso vipaścitaḥ" (RV 9.62.25). The *yaudhājaya* is "pra soma devavītaye" (RV 9.1.1). The *auśana* is "pra tu drava" (RV 9.43.1), which is the last. All [these] consist of three verses (*tṛca*). In the *ārbhava* [pavamāna], the *gāyatrasaṃhitā* is "svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā" (RV 8.48.1).

With the verses "Flow on with this" and "Flow on," there are single-verse hymns at the Saphākṣara; "He who presses" is the Gaurīvita for one verse; the Gautama for three verses; and the Kava is the final one. Everything else is like the first day. Everything is fifteen-fold. The second day is according to the archetype.

For the third day: *tantvā nṛmṇāni* consists of five verses; there is an omission (*uddhāra*) of the last two verses because of the impossibility of the *stoma*. *abhisomā*, *paurumadga*, *gautama*, *āṣkāraṇidhana*, and *kāṇva* are the triple-verse *sāmans*. *Antarikṣa* is performed on three verses. In the *ārbhava* [laud], the *vācaḥsāma*, *śaukta*, and *gaurīvitāni* are single-verse *sāmans*. Everything else is like the third day. Everything is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*).

For the fourth day: *pratājījanat prayadgāḥ* is the ṣaḍṛca-stotra. They perform the *bahispavamāna*. At the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*), on the *bṛhatī* verses, there are the *sāmatṛcas* consisting of the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*, *uttarābhīśu*, *uttarasvaḥ*, *pṛṣṭha*, and *āṅgirasa* chants; this is because of the statement that "three of these should be combined in whichever [verse] is possible. At the third pressing (*ārbhava*), the *ekarcas* are the *bṛhat*, *kātyā*, *iṣādīyat*, and *ānadānya*. Everything else is like the fourth day. All [stomas] are fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*), as is the *ṣoḍaśin* chant.

For the fifth day: *govid*, *viśvavid*, and *dadhanviṣu* constitute the seven-verse [stotra]. *yāste dhārāḥ* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. In the seven-verse [stotra], there is an omission (*uddhāra*) of the final verse because of the impossibility of the *stoma*. *arṣā soma* is for the two triplets in *gāyatrī* and *anuṣṭubh* meters. *soma uṣva* constitutes the *mānava*, *anūpa*, and *vāma* triplets of *sāmans*. *agneḥ triṇidhanam* is performed on three verses. *yat soma citram* is the *śaiśava*, the final [stotra] of the midday pressing, performed on three verses. In the *ārbhava* [pressing], *asāvyaṃśurmadāya* is the *gāyatra-saṃtaninī*.

The two single-verse hymns *abhi dyumnam* and *prāṇā śiśuḥ* are used in the *cyāvana-krośa*; *pavasva vājasātaye* is the *gaurīvita* on one verse; the *ṛṣabha-śākvara* is on three verses; and *induḥ vājī* is the final *dāśaspatya* of the *ārbhava* on three verses. Everything else is like the fifth day; everything is fifteen-fold.

The Sixth Chapter: Variations of the Twelve-Day Rite; the Sixth Day. The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant consists of the first six verses of the ten-verse hymn beginning with "He has created light, stars, and rest" (*jyotir asṛkṣad vīti*). The verse "To Indra, O Indu" (*indrāyendava*) is sung in the *gāyatra* melody on a single verse. The three-verse chants (*sāmatṛca*) are: the *iṣovṛdhīya*, the *krauñca*, and the *vājadāvarya*. The *revatī* verses are sung on three verses. The *svāra* chant begins with "Being cleansed by the skillful hand" (*mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya*), using the *aukṣṇorandhra* and *aiḍamaukṣṇorandhra* melodies on the first verse. The three-verse chants (*sāmatṛca*) are: the *vājajit*, the *varuṇasāma*, and the *goṣṭha*. The final chant is the *vāmadevya* melody on the verse "This one indeed" (*etamu tyam*), sung in the *ihavat* manner.

In the Ārbhava [Śastra], there are two triplets consisting of the Āida and Krauñca Sāmans; the others consist of single verses (ekarcas). Everything else is like the sixth day; everything is fifteenfold (pañcadaśa).

On the seventh day: for the *bahiṣpavamāna*, the nine-verse hymn beginning with "pra kāvyam" (starting with *ā te dakṣam*) is used; for the *gāyatrasaṃtanī*, the *vṛṣā pavasva* hymn; and for the triple-verses (*tṛca*), the *aiḍa*, *sauparṇa*, and others. For the *sāmatṛcas*, there are the *kaṇvarathantara*, *gauṅgava*, *sāptamika*, *āyāsya*, and others, beginning with "punānaḥ soma. For the final *mādhyaṃdina* [stotra], the *pravad-bhārgava* beginning with "pro ayāsīt. In the *ārbhava*, the *gāyatra*, *agnerarka*, *adhyardha*, *aiḍa*, *somasaṃjñaka*, and other *sāmatṛcas*. For the two single verses, the *śārkaraplava* hymns beginning with "eṣa sya sakhāya."

"Purojitī" is for Gaurīvita on one verse; "Kārtayaśam" is for three verses; "Pravājyakṣa" is for Sauhaviṣa on three verses; "Ye somāsaḥ" is for Jarābodhīya, the final [stotra] of the Ārbhava Pavamāna, on three verses. Everything else is like that of the seventh day. Thus is the fifteenth [day].

For the eighth day: the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant begins with "These Somas for the Child" (*śiśumete somābhinavaḥ*) and "Flow on with this hymn" (*ayā pavasva*). Then follow the *gāyatravilamba* and *sauparṇa* chants with "O Adhvaryu, the Soma pressed with stones" (*adhvaryo adribhiḥ sutam*). The *dvihiṃkāra-vāmadevya* and *acchidra* chants begin with "Toward the Soma" (*abhi soma*). The final *mādhyaṃdina* chant is the *udvat-bhārgava* beginning with "The Supporter of Heaven" (*dhartā divaḥ*). For the *ārbhava-pavamāna*, the *sāmatṛcas* (stotriyas) consist of the *gāyatra*, *svāśira*, *arkagāyatrī*, and *āsita* chants, beginning with "Flow on, O God, in due order" (*pavasva deva ānuṣak*). The *aiṣira* and *atra* chants, consisting of single verses (*ekarcas*), begin with "Toward glory" (*abhi dyumnam*) and "The Child, the vital breaths" (*prāṇā śiśuḥ*).

"Abhi no vājasātamaṃ" is the Gaurīvita [Sāman] on one verse; the Aiḍakautsa on three verses; the Svāsu-dharma on three verses; "Hinvanti sūraṃ" is the Viśoviśīya, the last [Sāman] of the Ārbhava [Pavamāna]; everything else is like that of the eighth day; all [the Stomas] are fifteenfold (pañcadaśa).

For the ninth day: *akrān eṣa devaḥ* and *pavamānasya te kavaḥ* constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*, consisting of nine verses; in the ten-verse version, the last verse is omitted. *pavamānasya jighnataḥ* are the two *gāyatra* verses. *parītoṣiṣe* are the three *sāman* triplets for the *pṛṣṭha* chants: the *kaulmalabarhiṣa* and the *saṃkṛti*. The *devasthāna* is performed on three verses. *asāvi somaḥ* is the final *arka* of Dīrghatamas, or alternatively, the *sāmarāja*.

The *sāman*s and *ṛc*s for the final section of the *Sāmarāja* are those of Parītoṣī, Pṛṣṭha, Dīrghatamas, Arka, and Māṇḍava; the *sāman*s and *ṛc*s for the [sections] of Dairghaśravasa, Saṃkṛti, and Devasthāna; the *sāman*s and *ṛc*s for the Gāyatra, Aśvasūkta, Pratīcīna, Aiḍa, and Kāśīta, beginning with "O Soma, you are the sustainer" (*tvaṃ soma asi dhārayuḥ*); the *sāman*s and *ṛc*s for the Suparṇa and Vaiśvamanasa, which consist of single verses beginning with "For you indeed, O divine one, flow for the feast of the gods" (*tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye*); the Gaurīvita on a single verse beginning with "Around him, the desirable, the golden" (*pari tyam haryataṃ hariṃ*); and the Yadvāhiṣṭhīya on three verses.

In his own [stomas], there are three *vidharma* [stotras]. The final [stotra] of the Ārbhava-pavamāna is the *upoṣya* [type], which is to be heard. Everything else is like the ninth day; everything is fifteenfold (*pañcadaśa*).

For the tenth day: "They have been let loose, the prize-winners... (RV 9.62.25), "The purifier, the all-knower... (RV 9.86.12), "The purifier has generated... (RV 9.96.5), and "These drops have been let loose... (RV 9.101.1)—these are single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*). "Flow on, O Indu, as a bull, pressed... (RV 9.97.1–3) is a triplet (*tṛca*). "Of this one, the ancient [songs]... (RV 9.107.1–9) is the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant; from the nine verses, the last one is omitted. "High up for thee... (RV 1.84.1–3) are the triplets for the *gāyatra*, *āmahīyava*, and *abhīka* *sāmans*. "Being purified, O Soma... (RV 9.1.1–6) is the sixth chapter. These are the variations for the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*).

The *utsedha*, *yajñāyajñīya*, and *niṣedha* [stotras] are performed on triplets (*tṛca*). The *gaurīvita* is the final [stotra] of the midday pressing, beginning with "ājāgṛvi. In the Ārbhava Pavamāna, the *gāyatra-saṃhita* consists of two triplets beginning with "svādiṣṭhya. The *sapha*, *rohita*, and *kuvalīya* consist of single verses (*ekarca*) beginning with "pavasvendramaccha. The *śyāvāśva* is on a single verse beginning with "paryuṣva. The *āndhīgava* is on three verses. The final [stotra] is the *vājajit* on verses containing the word "sūya. Everything else is like the tenth day. Everything is fifteen-fold (*pañcadaśa*). The ten duties (*daśamadharmāḥ*) should be performed with a unified mind. 5.
[The third twelve-day rite with the seventeen-fold stoma]:
He speaks of the twelve-day rite with the seventeen-fold stoma—
just as the third [rite].
Thus it is to be explained as before. ||6||
He states the qualified person: "Therefore, one who desires consecration or one who desires progeny [should perform it]. (7)

Thus it is said. The word "one should sacrifice" (*yajeta*) is understood to carry over. Regarding that, for the first day: *asya pratnā* (nine verses), *pavasvāpa* (five verses), and *pavamānasya te kava* constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. *Pra somāso vipaścitaḥ* and the *gāyatrāśvasoma-sāmans* are performed on the three-verse stanzas (*tṛcas*). *Pra soma devavītaye* is the *gauṅgava* on one verse; the *pajra* is on that same verse. The *yaudhājaya* is on three verses; the final *auśana* is on three verses. In the *ārbhava-pavamāna*, *svādiṣṭhayā* and the *gāyatrasaṃhitas* are on two sets of three verses.

With the two single-verse hymns beginning "Flow on" (*ayā pavasva*) and "The beloved one flows, the golden one" (*pavate haryate hariḥ*), [the stotras are formed]. With the three-verse hymns beginning "Pressed out" (*pra sunvānaḥ*), [they are formed] for the Gaurīvita and Gautama [sāmans]. The final [stotra] is the Kāva. Everything else is like the first day. Everything is seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*).

For the second day: *pavasva vācaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā soma*, and *utte śu*—these five verses [constitute] the *bahippavamāna*. With the verse *vṛṣā pavasva*, there are two *gāyatrī* stanzas for the *uktāśva* chant. For the *samantadairghaśravasa* chant, the first [verse] is used. For the *aiḍamāyāsya* and *atriṇidhana* chants, the two triplets are used. *Vṛṣā śoṇaḥ* is the final [verse] of the *vāsiṣṭha* chant. When performing [the rite] with single-verse units, one should place them at the beginning of the first [day], because of the statement: "Two [verses] in that very [first day]."

"At the Ārbhava Pavamāna, [the verses] 'Flow toward Indra' and 'Go toward Indra' consist of single verses when the *śaṅku* is well-known; the others are triplets (*tṛca*). Everything else is like the second day."
The third day is according to the archetype.

For the fourth day: *prataḥ* [is the stotriya]; *ajījanat prayad gāḥ* is the *ṣaḍṛca*; *āśuḥ* is the *ṣaḍṛca*; the first three verses form the *tṛca*; *hinvanti sūram* is the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant. In the *ṣaḍṛca*, there is the omission (*uddhāra*) of the final verse because of the impossibility of the *stoma*. At the midday pressing, on the *bṛhatī* meter, *tavāham some* is [the stotriya] on the first of the two verses beginning with *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra* and *uttarābhīśava*. On the *svar-sāman*, the *pṛṣṭhāṅgirasa* is performed on three verses. At the third pressing, the *bṛhat* and *kātyāyanīya* are on two single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*). Everything else is like the fourth day. All [stomas] are seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*), and there is also the *ṣoḍaśin* sāman.

For the fifth day: *govit*, *viśvavit*, and *dhanvit*—these seven-versed [stotras]; for the *bahiṣpavamāna*: *yavaṃ-yavam naḥ*, *yā te dhārā*. In the four-versed [form], there is the omission (*uddhāra*) of the last three, because it is seen thus in the *Aupaśada* and because of the impossibility of the *stoma*. For the *gāyatra* and *ṛkva*: *arṣā soma*; for the *mānava* and *ānūpa*: *soma uṣva*. In the first [verse] of these three, the *vāma* [melody]; in the [other] three, the *agni-triṇidhana*. For the final three of the midday [service]: *yat soma citram*, the *śaiśava* melody.

In the Ārbhava [Śastra], for the two triplets, there are the *Gāyatra-saṃtaninī* verses beginning with "āsuṣvayaṃśuḥ" and "abhidyumnam". In the *Cyāvana-krośa*, for the two single verses, there are those beginning with "prāṇāḥ" and "śiśuḥ".

The sixth day—The variations of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*): For the *Ārbhava*, the Sāman triplets are the *Gaurīvita*, *Ṛṣabha*, *Śākvara*, and *Pārtha*, beginning with "pavasva vājasātaye". There is an eightfold *iḍā-pada-stobha* on three verses. The final verse of the *Ārbhava* is the *Dāśaspatya* beginning with "indurvājī". Everything else is like the fifth day. Everything is seventeen-fold (*saptadaśa*).

For the sixth day: *Jyotir asṛkṣata* (The light has been emitted) is the ten-verse *bahiṣpavamāna*; from this [set of] ten verses, the last two are omitted because of the impossibility of the *stoma*. For the two triplets, *indrāyendavaḥ* are the *gāyatrī* and *revatī* verses. *Mṛjyamānaḥ* is the *svāra-sāman* on the first verse of the *aukṣṇorandhra-iḍa-aukṣṇorandhra* [tune]. *Vājajit* and *goṣṭha* are for the two triplets. *Etamu tyam* is the final *vāmadevya* containing the word *iha*. In the *ārbhava-pavamāna*, *parisvānaḥ* is the *gāyatra-sāman* on three verses.

The third [day] belongs to Vaidanvata and consists of three [stotras]. *Sa sunva vaḥ sakha* is for Dīrghatamas Kārṇaśravasa and consists of two single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*). *Somāḥ pavante* contains the Gaurīvita, Madhuścunnidhana, Vāṅnidhana, and Krauñca Sāmans, each consisting of three verses (*sāmatṛcas*). The Aiḍakrauñca is performed on three verses. *Ayā pavasva pavasva* is the Śnauṣṭa, the last [Sāman], performed on three verses. Everything else is like the sixth day. All [the stomas] are seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*).

For the seventh day: *prakāprasvānavarcam*, *ete asṛgram*, and *ā te dakṣam* for the *bahiṣpavamāna*. In the nine-verse [stoma], there is an omission (*uddhāra*) of the final verse. For the *vṛṣā pavasva* [stotra], there are the *gāyatras*, *santanyas*, *aiḍas*, and *sauvarṇas*. For *punānaḥ soma*, the *kaṇvarathantara* is used on the first verse. On that same verse, the *gauṅgava* with two finales (*dvinidhana*), the *āyāsya*, is used on three verses. Then follows *pro ayāsīt*.

The *prastāva* is the *bhārgava*; the *mādhyaṃdina* [stotra] ends with [the verse] "yaste madaḥ. The *gāyatra*, *agni-arka*, *adhyardha-iḍa*, and *soma-sāman* are the *sāmatṛcas*. The *śārkaraplava* [sāmans] are on two single verses: "eṣa sya dhārayā" and "sakhāya ā niṣīdata. The *purojitī* [sāman] is the *gaurīvitakārtayaśa* on two triplets. The *sauhaviṣa* [sāman] is "pra vājyakṣa" on three verses. The *jarābodhīya*, the last of the *ārbhava* [stotra], is "ye somāsaḥ. Everything else is like the seventh day; everything is seventeenfold.

For the eighth day: "These Somas for the Child" (*śiśumete somā*) is the *navarca*; "Upward for you, O Lord" (*utteśa*) is the *pañcarca*; and "Flow with this stream" (*ayā pavasva dhārayā*) is the *bahis-pavamāna*. From the *navarca*, one should extract the final triplet. At the midday pressing: "O Adhvaryu, with the stones" (*adhvaryo adribhiḥ*) is the *gāyatra-vilamba-sauparṇa*; "The Soma-drops, the Āyus" (*abhisomāsa āyavaḥ*) is the *vāmadevya* with two *hiṅkāras* on the first verse; the *hārāyaṇācchidra* is on the two triplets; the *bārhaduktha* is on the middle verse; and "The upholder of heaven" (*dhartā divaḥ*) is the final *udvat-bhārgava*.

"Flow for the Ārbhava, O God, bestowing long life"—this Gāyatra chant is performed on three verses. The *Svāśira*, *Arkya*, *Kākṣīvata*, and *Bhāsa* are the *sāman*-verses (*sāmatṛcas*). "Toward glory, toward breath, the infant"—these are the *aiṣira* chants on two single-verse stanzas (*ekarcas*). "Toward us, the most excellent winner of booty"—the *Gaurīvita*, *Rayiṣṭha*, and *Audala* are the *sāman*-verses. On their own [verses], there are three [stanzas] for the *Dharma*. "They urge on the Sun"—this is the *Viśoviśīya*, the final [chant] of the Ārbhava. Everything else is like the eighth day. All [the stomas] are seventeenfold (*saptadaśa*).

For the ninth day: *akrān eṣa devaḥ* is a hymn of ten verses; *eṣa u sya vṛṣā* is a hymn of one verse; and *pavamānasya te kavaḥ* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. The *sāman*-verses for the *gāyatras*, *ādārasṛt*, *ṛṣabha*, and *pavamāna* are [based on] *pavamānasya jighnate*. The *pṛṣṭha* [stotra] is based on *parītoṣi* performed on a single verse. The *saṃkṛti*, *devasthāna*, *abhīśava*, and others are performed on triplets (*tṛcas*). The *vāsiṣṭha* is performed on the *adhyāsyā* verse. *asāvi somaḥ* is the final *arka* of Dīrghatamas, or alternatively, the *sāmarāja*.
In the alternative where the *sāmarāja* is last, the *pṛṣṭha-dīrghatama-arka* and the *māṇḍavas* take the place of the *pṛṣṭha*.

The Sixth Chapter: Variations of the Twelve-Day Rite; Sāmans and Triads of Verses. The *ābhīśava* and others are performed on a single verse. The *devasthāna* is on three verses. The *saṃkṛti* is on three verses. The *vāsiṣṭha* is on the middle verse. In the *ārbhava* [laud], the *gāyatra* "tvam soma" is on three verses. The *āśvasūkta*, *pratīcīna*, *iḍāṅka*, *āśīta*, and *hāviṣkṛta* are *sāman*-triads. The *sauparṇa* and *vaiśvamanasa* "tvam hy aṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye" are on two single verses.

The *sāman*-verses beginning with "pari tyam haryatam harim" are the Gaurīvita-nihnavayadvāhiṣṭhīyas; they are performed on their own three verses beginning with "vidharma. The final verse of the Ārbhava-pavamāna, "upo ṣu jātam," is the Śrudhya. Everything else is like the ninth day; everything is seventeenfold.

For the tenth day: *asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*, *pavamānasya viśvavit*, *pavamāno ajījanat*, *ete asṛgram indavaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā sutaḥ*—these five are single-verse hymns (*ekarcāḥ*). *asya pratnā* is a nine-verse hymn. *pavamānasya te kavaḥ* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. For the two triplets of the *gāyatrāmahīyava* chants, [the verses are] *uccā te jātam andhasaḥ*. For the first [triplet], *punānaḥ soma* is the *rauravotsedha*. For the two triplets, *yajñīyajñīya* is the *niṣedha*.

The *ājāgṛvi* [verse] belongs to Gaurīvita; it is the final [stotra] of the midday pressing. At the third pressing (*ārbhava*), the two triplets are the *svādiṣṭhya* [verse] for the Gāyatra-saṃhita. The two single verses are the *pavasva indram accha* [verse] for the Sapha and Rohitakūlīya. The triplet of Sāmans is the *pary ū ṣu* [verse] for Śyāvāśva’s Auṣṇiha, the Ekanidhana, and the Āndhīgava. The *paripradhanva* [verse] is the Sauhaviṣa for three verses. The final [stotra] of the third pressing is the Vājajit. Everything else is like the tenth day. Everything is seventeenfold. The rules of the tenth day are to be performed with the same Sāman. 7.
[The Twelfth-Day Rite with the Twenty-onefold Stoma,
the Fourth] He speaks of the Twelfth-Day Rite with the Twenty-onefold Stoma:
"Just as the fourth."
Thus; it is to be explained as before. ||8||
He states the qualified person: "By that, one who desires consecration [is the qualified person]. (9)

Thus it is said. "One should sacrifice" (*yajeta*) is understood to carry over. This is its arrangement. Regarding that, for the first day: *asya pratnā* is the nine-verse hymn; *ete somā abhi* is the nine-verse hymn; and *pavamānasya te kava* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. The additions and omissions (*āva* and *udvāpa*) should be made according to the *stomas*, as in the *ādityānām ayana*, the *chandoga*, and the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*). At the midday pressing: *pra somāso vipaścitaḥ* are the *gāyatra*, *aśva*, and *soma-sāmans*. *Pra soma devavītaye* are the *gauṅgava*, *pajra*, and *audhājaya*s. The *auśana* is the last. All are three-verse hymns (*tṛca*s).

In the Ārbhava Pavamāna, [the verses] beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā" are in the Gāyatra-Saṃhitā meters; "ayā pavasva," "pavate haryataḥ," and "hariḥ" are in the Sapha-Akṣara meters, each consisting of a single verse (*ekarca*). "Prasunvānaḥ" is the Gaurīvita melody on a single verse. The Gautama, Śuddhāśuddhīya, and Sādhrāṇa melodies are used on triplets (*tṛca*). The last [verse] belongs to the Kava family. Everything else is like that of the first day. All [the stotras] consist of twenty-one verses.

For the second day: *pavasva vācaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā soma*, *vṛṣā hyasi*, and *eṣa u ṣaḍṛcam*; for the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant, [the verses] beginning with *pavamānasya te kava*. At the midday pressing, the *gāyatra*, *ukta-aśva*, and *svāra* chants are used, beginning with *vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā*. This is the sixth chapter: the twelve variations of the *dvādaśaha*, the *sauparṇa* hymns. For the *ārbhava-pavamāna*: *punānaḥ soma* is the *aiḍa*, *āyāsya*, *triṇidhana*, *āyāsya-samanta* chants; *vṛṣā śoṇaḥ* is the final *vāsiṣṭha*. All [stotras] at the *ārbhava* are in three-verse (*tṛca*) units. Everything else is like the second day. Everything is in the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) stoma.

For the third day: *davidyutatyā* (SV 1.267), *ete rājā* (SV 1.270), *tantvā nṛmṇāni* (SV 1.273)—this constitutes a five-verse hymn; *yavaṃ yavam* (SV 1.278)—a four-verse hymn; and *iṣe* (SV 1.282) for the *vahiṣpavamāna*. For the *ārbhava-pavamāna*: *uccā te jātam* (SV 1.459) contains the *gāyatra*, *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*, and *paurumadga* chants; *abhi somāsaḥ* (SV 1.462) contains the *gautama*, *antarikṣa*, and *āṣkāraṇidhana* chants upon three verses each; and *tisro vācaḥ* (SV 1.465) contains the final *aṅgirasāṃ saṃkrośa*. In the *ārbhava-pavamāna*, all [verses] consist of triplets (*tṛca*). Everything else is like the third day. All [stomas] are twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*).
The fourth day is according to the archetype.

For the fifth day: *govit*, *viśvavit*, and *dadhad*—these are the seven verses for the *dhanvan* [stoma]; *ut te śu* is the five-verse [stotra]; and *yās ta* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. At the midday [pressing]: *arṣā soma* and so forth are the *gāyatra*, *anvaśākala*, and *vārṣa* [sāmans]; *soma u ṣv* and so forth are the *mānava*, *ānūpa*, and *vāma* triads of *sāmans*; and the *triṇidhana* of Agni is performed on three verses. *yat soma citram* is the final *śaiśava* [sāman]. At the third pressing (*ārbhava*): *asāvyaṃśuḥ* is the *gāyatra-saṃtaninī*.

*Abhi dyumnam*, *prāṇāḥ*, and *śiśuḥ* are for the *cyāvana-krośa* in the two single-verse hymns; *pavasva vājasātaye* is the *gaurīvita* in one verse; the *ṛṣabha*, *śākvara*, *pārtha*, *aṣṭa*, *iḍāpada*, and *stobha* are in the triple-verse hymns; *induḥ vājī* is the final *dāśaspatya*; everything else is like the fifth day; all [the stotras] are twenty-one-fold.

For the sixth day: *jyotirasṛkṣata vīrayati* is a hymn of ten verses; *taratsamandī* is a hymn of four verses; and *ete somāsaḥ* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. At the midday pressing: *indāyendavaḥ* is the *gāyatra-raivata*; *mṛjyamānaḥ* is the *svāra-aukṣṇorandhra-vājajit-varuṇasāma-goṣṭha* on three triplets; and *etamu tyam* is the final *ihavat-vāmadevya*. At the third pressing: *parisvānaḥ* consists of the *gāyatra*, the third [verse], the first, the fourth, and the *vaivanvatāni*.

The *sakhāya ā śiṣāmahi* [is used] for Dīrghatamas Śrautas; the *somāḥ pavante* [is used] for Gaurīviti in the first [verse]. There are the *madhuścun*, *nidhanavāṅnidhana*, *krauñca*, and *aiḍakrauñca* *sāman*-verses. The *ayā pavasva pāvasva* [is used]; the *śnauṣṭa* is the last. Everything else is like the sixth day. All [the days] are the twenty-one-fold [stoma].

For the seventh day: *prakāprasvānavarcam*; *asṛgran* consisting of nine verses; for the *bahiṣpavamāna*, [the hymn] beginning with *ā te dakṣam*. In the *asṛgran* hymn of nine verses, one should exclude the final triplet. At the midday pressing, one should exclude the *rohitakūlīya*. At the third pressing, the *gāyatra* beginning with *yaste madaḥ*, the *aukṣasoma* chants, and the *sāmatṛcas*. The *arkam* of Agni in three verses; or alternatively, the *gāyatra* in three verses; the *adhyardheḍa* chant of the *arkam* of Agni, the *aukṣa* chants, and the *sāmatṛcas*.

The *dhārayā* hymn, beginning with "eṣa sya," belongs to Śārkaraplava; it is for two single-verse stanzas. The *purojitī* hymn belongs to Gaurīvita; it is for one single-verse stanza. The *gautama* and *kārtayaśa* hymns are for two triple-verse stanzas. The *pravājyakṣa* hymn belongs to Sauhaviṣa; it is for three verses. The *jarābodhīya* hymn, beginning with "ye some," is the final one. Everything else is like that of the seventh day; everything is [performed] in the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) manner.

For the eighth day: "These Somas for the Child" (*śiśum ete somābhi*) is the *navarca* hymn; "Flow onward, O dispeller" (*ayāvy apaghnanayā pavasva dhārayā*) is the *bahispavamāna*. At the midday pressing: "O Adhvaryu, with the stones" (*adhvaryo adribhiḥ*) are the *gāyatra*, *vairūpa*, *āśubha*, and *bhārgava* [stotras]. "Toward us, O Soma" (*abhi soma*) are the *dvihiṃkāra*, *vāmadevya*, *gāyatra*, *pārśva*, and *pauruhanmana* [stotras]. "The upholder of heaven" (*dhartā divaḥ*) is the final *udvat* and *bhārgava*. All [these] consist of three verses (*tṛca*). At the third pressing: "Flow onward, O God, for life" (*pavasva deva āyuṣag*) is the *gāyatra* performed on three verses.

The *sāman*-verses are: the *svāśira*, *arka*, *kākṣīvata*, and *bhāsā*; the *abhidyumna*, *prāṇa*, and *āśu* [are] in the *aiṣira*; these two are single-verse (*ekarca*) [sāmans]. The *gaurīvita* is on the first verse of "abhī no vājasātama"; the *aiḍa*, *kautsa*, *padanidhana*, *śuddhāśuddhīya*, *krauñca*, and others are *sāman*-verses; the *rayiṣṭha* is on three verses; the *dharma* is on its own three verses; the *viśoviśīya* is the last; everything else is like the eighth day; all is twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*).

For the ninth day: *akrān eṣa devaḥ* is the nine-verse hymn; *eṣa u ṣaḍṛcam* is the six-verse hymn. *pavamānasya te kavaḥ* is the Bahiṣpavamāna; in the ten-verse version, the last verse is omitted. At the midday pressing, *pavamānasya jighnataḥ* is the Gāyatra triplet. *adārasṛt*, *iḍānām saṃkṣāraḥ*, *ṛṣabha*, and *pavamāna* are the three-verse Sāmans. *parītoṣi* contains the Pṛṣṭha, Kaulmalabarhiṣa, Saṃkṛti, and Devasthāna Sāmans in triplets. *jasāvi soma* is the final Arcika of Dīrghatamas, or alternatively, the Sāmarāja.

In the *sāmarāja* chant during the final section of the midday pressing, in place of the *pṛṣṭha-stotra*, there are the *sāmatṛcas* of the *arkamāṇḍava* belonging to Pṛṣṭha-Dīrghatamas. In the *ārbhava* [pressing], there is the *gāyatra* chant "tvaṃ some" on three verses. There are the *sāmatṛcas* of the *āśvasūkta*, the *pratīcīna*, the *iḍaṅka*, the *āśīta*, and the *hāviṣkṛta*. For the two single-verse chants (*ekarcas*), there are the *sauparṇa* and *vaiśvamanasa* chants beginning with "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye. The *gaurīvita* chant "pari tyaṃ haryataṃ hariṃ" is for the first verse. The *nihavayadvāhiṣṭhīya*, *āsita*, and others are the *sāmatṛcas*.
The *sādhra* is in three [verses]; the *vidharma* is in its own [verses], in three; "upo ṣvit" is the *śrudhya*; everything else is like the ninth day; everything is twenty-one-fold.

For the tenth day: "They have been let loose, the prize-winners... (*asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*), "The purifier, the all-knowing... (*pavamānasya viśvavit*), and "The purifier has brought forth... (*pavamāno ajījanat*)—these three are single-verse hymns (*ekarcāḥ*). "These have been let loose... (*ete asṛgram*), and "Flow on, O Indu, as a bull, being pressed... (*pavasvendo vṛṣā sutaḥ*)—these two are triple-verse hymns (*tṛcau*). "His ancient [songs]... (*asya pratnā*) is a nine-verse hymn. "O Purifier, of thee... (*pavamānasya te kava*) is the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant. At the midday pressing: "Upward for thee... (*uccā te*) constitutes the *gāyatra*, *āmahīyava*, and *abhīka* chants. "Being purified, O Soma... (*punānaḥ soma*) includes the *utsedha*, *yajñāyajñīya*, and *niṣedha* chants. "Awake, O hero... (*ā jāgṛvir*) is the *gaurīvita* chant, which is the final one.

In the *ārbhava* [laud], the two *gāyatra-saṃhita* verses are "svādiṣṭhayā" and "pavasva indram accha. The two *sapha-rohitakūlīya* verses are "pary ū ṣu. The *sāmatṛcas*—namely the *śyāvāśva-auṣṇiha*, the *ekonidhana*, and the *āndhīgava*—are performed with the verse "pary ū ṣu. The *sauhaviṣa* is performed on three verses beginning with "pari pra dhanva. The final [verse] is the *vājajit* containing the word "sūrya. Everything else is like the tenth day. The entire twenty-first day is identical; the rules of the tenth day are to be applied in common.
