Regarding the Tṛṇavastomadvādaśāha, he says: "As in the fifth. 10.
Thus; it is to be explained as before.
He states the qualified practitioner: "By that [rite], one desiring nourishment, or wishing to slay an enemy. (11)
The sixth chapter: "The variations of the twelve-day rite.

This is clear. Its arrangement is like that of the Chandoma ten-night rite of the Ādityānām Ayana; the insertion (*āvāpa*) and deletion (*udvāpa*) of elements should be performed in accordance with the *stomas*.

Regarding that, for the first day: "Asya pratnā" is a nine-verse hymn; "Ete somā abhi" is a nine-verse hymn; "Somaḥ punānaḥ" is a nine-verse hymn—these constitute the Bahiṣpavamāna. At the midday [Pavamāna]: "Pra somāso vipaścitaḥ" includes the Gāyatra, Aśvasoma, Sāman, and Āśubhārgava hymns; "Pra soma devavītaye" includes the Pajra, Dvaigata, Gauṅgava, and Audhājaya hymns; the Auśana is the final one. All are triplets (tṛca). At the Ārbhava [Pavamāna]: "Svādiṣṭhayā" includes the Gāyatra, Saṃhita, and Jarābodhīya hymns.

With the verses "Flow on, seeking the gods" (*ayā pavasva devayuḥ*) and "He flows" (*pavate*), there are two single-verse hymns at the *saphākṣara* [stotra]. With the verse "Pressed forth" (*pra sunvānaḥ*), there is the *gaurīvitam* at one [verse]. There are the *vaiśvāmitra-padanidhana*, the *śuddhāśuddhīya*, the *svāra*, the *kautsa*, and the *gautama*. The *kāva* is the final [hymn]. Everything else is like the first day. All [the stotras] consist of the *triṇava* [stoma].

For the second day: *pavasva vācaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā soma vṛṣā hyasi*—this is the six-verse [stotra]. *Eṣa vājī* is the six-verse [stotra]. For the *bahiṣpavamāna*: *pavamānasya te vayam*. At the midday [pressing], for the *gāyatra* [stoma]: *vṛṣā pavasva*; the *ukta-aśva*, *surūpa*, and *hariśrī* are the *nidhanas*. For the *samanta-dairghaśravasa* [stomas]: *punānaḥ soma*; the *aiḍa-māyāsya* and *triṇidhana-māyāsya* [are the *nidhanas*]. *Vṛṣā śoṇaḥ* is the final [stotra] belonging to the Vasiṣṭhas. All [these stotras] consist of triplets (*tṛcas*).

In the Ārbhava [Śastra], "yaste madaḥ" is for Gāyatra; "pavasvendram accha" is for Śaṅku and Sujñāna; "ayaṃ pūṣā" consists of the [hymns] of Gaurīviti, Kutsa, Bharga, and Krauñca; "vṛṣā matīnām" is the final [hymn] of Yāma. All are triplets (tṛcas). Everything else is like the second day. Everything is the Triṇava [stoma].

On the third day: *davidyutatyā*, *ete*, *rājā tantum*, and *paṅkti*—this constitutes the five-verse hymn; *eṣa dhiyā* is the eight-verse hymn; and *apaghnann iṣe pavasva* is the Bahiṣpavamāna stotra. In the eight-verse hymn, the last verse is omitted. At the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*), there are the *gāyatra*, *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*, *saumitra*, and *aiṭata* chants; *abhi soma* includes the *paurumadga*, *gautama*, *antarikṣa*, *āṣkāraṇidhana*, and *kāṇva* chants; and *tisro vācaḥ* is the final *aṅgirasām-saṃkrośa*.

In the Ārbhava [Śastra], there are three verses beginning with *vācaḥ*. These include the Gāyatra, Pāṣṭha, Auḍuṅga, and Saindhukṣita [Sāmans]. The Vācaḥsāman and Śaukta [Sāmans] are based on the verse beginning with *ā sotā sakhāyaḥ*. The Gaurīvita, Aiḍa, Tvāṣṭrīsāman, Triṇidhana, and [another] Tvāṣṭrīsāman are based on the verse beginning with *sutāsoma*. The verse beginning with *pavitraṃ te* has the Ariṣṭa as its final [Sāman]. Everything else is like that of the third day. All [the Stomas] are Triṇava.

For the fourth day: *pra ta ajījanata pra yad gāḥ*—this is the six-verse hymn (*ṣaḍṛca*). *Āśuḥ*—this is the six-verse hymn. *Hinvanti*—this is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. At the midday pressing: *pavasva dakṣasādhana*—these are the [stotras] having the *gāyatra*, *ātharvaṇa*, *nidhana-kāma*, *tavāham some*, *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*, *uttarārka*, *puṣpa*, *ādyabārhaduktha*, *abhīśava*, *ādyasvaḥpṛṣṭha*, and *āṅgirasa* [tunes]. *Punānaḥ*—the *satrāsāhīya* is the final [stotra]. All [of these] consist of three verses (*tṛca*).

In the Ārbhava [Śastra], the verses beginning with "pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" are in the Gāyatrī metre; the *ūrṇāyava*, *bṛhat*, *bhāradvāja*, *nidhana*, and *mārgīyava* [stotriyas] are used. The verses beginning with "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā" are in the Bṛhat [metre] according to the Kātīṣādīya school. The verses beginning with "purojitī" are in the Nānada and Andhīgava [melodies]. The verse beginning with "somaḥ pavate" is the final *janitra*. All [these stotriyas] consist of triplets (*tṛca*). Everything else is like that of the fourth day. All [the Śastras] are *triṇava*; and so is the *ṣoḍaśin* Sāman.
The fifth day is according to the original model.

For the sixth day: *jyotirasṛkṣata* and *vīrayati*, each consisting of ten verses; *sanā* consisting of ten verses. Thus ends the sixth chapter: *ete some*. There are two variations for the *bahiṣpavamāna* of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*). In the *vīrayati* hymn of ten verses, there is the extraction (*uddhāra*) of the penultimate and final verses. For the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*), the triplet-sāmans are: *mṛjyamānaḥ* as *svāra*, *aukṣṇorandhra*, and *aiḍamaukṣṇorandhravājajit*. The others are triplets (*tṛca*). For the third pressing (*ārbhava*), the *dīrghakārṇaśravasa* and *gaurīvita* are single-verse hymns (*ekarca*). The others are triplets. Everything else is like the sixth day. All [the stomas] are the *triṇava*.

On the seventh day: *prakā prasva* is a hymn of nine verses; *asṛgran* is a hymn of nine verses; *yavaṃ yavam* is a hymn of four verses. The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant begins with *ā te dakṣam*. In the four-verse hymn, the last verse is omitted. At the midday pressing, the *gāyatrasaṃtani*, *aiḍa*, *sauparṇa*, and *rohitakūlīya* [stotras] begin with *vṛṣā pavasva*. The *kaṇvarathantara*, *paurumadga*, *gauṅgava*, *vinidhana*, and *māyāsya* [stotras] begin with *punānaḥ soma*. The *pravadbhārgava* begins with *pro āyāsīt*; this is the final one. All [these stotras] consist of triplets (*tṛca*).
In the Ārbhava Pavamāna, the Gautama hymn follows the Kārtayaśa; everything else is like the seventh day. Everything is the Triṇava stoma.

On the eighth day: for the *śiśu* [stotra], the nine-verse hymn beginning with "these Somas"; for the *soma*, the nine-verse hymn beginning with "purifying himself"; and for the *bahiṣpavamāna*, the verse beginning with "flowing away, flow pure with your stream. At the midday pressing: for the *gāyatra-vairūpa-aśubha-bhārgava-vilamba-sauparṇa* [stotras], the verses beginning with "O Adhvaryu, with the stones"; for the *abhi soma* [stotra], the *dvihiṃkāra-vāmadevya-gāyatrapārśva-hārāyaṇa-pauruhanmana* [stotras]; and for the *udvat-bhārgava* [stotra], the final verse beginning with "the upholder of heaven. At the third pressing: for the *ārbhava* [stotra], the *gāyatra* [stotra] consisting of three verses beginning with "flow pure, O God, for the sake of life."

The *sāman*-verses are *svāśira*, *arka*, *kākṣīvata*, and *bhāsā*; *abhi dyumnam*, *prāṇāḥ*, and *śiśuḥ*—these belong to the *aiṣira*. *Abhī no vājasātamam* belongs to the *gaurīvita*, *aiḍa*, *kautsa*, and *audala* [schools]. In their own [verses], the *dharma* is "hinvanti"; the last [verse] is the *viśoviśīya*. Everything else is like the eighth day; everything is the *triṇava* [stoma].

For the ninth day: *ākrān*—this is the ten-verse hymn; *eṣa dhiyā*—this is the eight-verse hymn. For the *vahiṣpavamāna*: *iṣe pavasva*, *pavamānasya te*, and *kava*. At the midday pressing: for the *gāyatra*, *ādārasṛj*, *iḍānīsaṃkṣāra*, *ṛṣabha*, and *pavamāna* chants, [the verses are] *pavamānasya jighnate*. For the *pṛṣṭha* stotras, the *kaulmalabarhiṣa*, *saṃkṛti*, and *devasthāna* chants begin with *parīto ṣi*.

The final *ṛk* of Dīrghatamas, "asāvi soma," is the *arka*; or it is the *sāmarāja*. In the latter view regarding the *sāmarāja*, at the midday pressing, in the place of the *pṛṣṭha-stotra*, there are the *pṛṣṭha-dīrghatama-arka-māṇḍava* *sāman*-verses (*sāmatṛcas*). At the third pressing (*ārbhava*), [the verses] are "tvaṃ soma" (Gāyatra), the Aśvasūkta, the Pratīcīna, the Aiḍa, and the Kāśīta; "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya pavasva devavītaye" (Sauparṇa-Vaiśvamanasa); "pari tyam" (Gaurīvita-Sādhrī); "svāsu vidharma"; and "upo ṣu" (Śrudhya) as the last. All are three-verse hymns (*tṛcas*). Everything else is like the ninth day. Everything is the Triṇava.

For the tenth day: *asṛkṣata pravājinah*, *pavamānasya viśvavit*, *pavamāno ajījanat*, *ete asṛgram indavaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā sutaḥ*, and *asya pratnām navarcam*—these constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. At the midday pressing: *uccā ta*, *gāyatrāmahīyavā-jigābhīkāni*, *punānaḥ soma*, *rauravotsedha-yajñāyajñīyaniṣedhāḥ*, and *ā jāgṛvir it* as the final *gaurīvita*; all [of these] consist of triplets (*tṛca*).

In the Ārbhava [Śastra], after the *saṃhitā*, there is the *surūpa* hymn; everything else is like the tenth day. Everything is *triṇava*. The duties of the tenth day are to be performed with a common *sāman*.
[The Twelve-Day Rite with the Trayastriṃśa Stoma,
the Sixth] He speaks of the twelve-day rite with the trayastriṃśa stoma—
just as the sixth.
Thus; it is to be explained as before. ||||
He states the qualified person: "Therefore, one who desires consecration [is the qualified person]."

Thus [it is said]. The word "one should sacrifice" (*yajeta*) is understood to carry over. Its ritual arrangement (*klṛpti*) is like that of the *ādityānām ayana* and the *chandoma-daśāha*. The insertion (*āvāpa*) and extraction (*udvāpa*) of verses should be performed according to the sequence of the *stomas*. Among these, for the first day: "His ancient splendor" (*asya pratnānu varam*), "These Soma-pressings, new splendor" (*ete somā abhi navarcam*), "Soma being purified, new splendor" (*somaḥ punāno navarcam*), and "Forward your streams, unceasing" (*pra te dhārā asaścutaḥ*). [This concludes] the sixth chapter of Pavamāna; [now follow] the variations of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*).

*Kava* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. In the four-verse [stoma], there is the omission of the final verse. At the midday pressing, *pra somāso vipaścitaḥ* consists of the Gāyatra, Aśvasoma, Sāman, and Āśubhārgava [Sāmans]. *Pra soma devavītaye* consists of the Pajra, Dvaigata, Dvihiṃkāra, Vāmadevya, Gauṅgava, Pauruhanmana, Yaudhājaya, and the final Auśana. At the third pressing (*ārbhava*), *svādiṣṭhayā* consists of the Gāyatra, Saṃhita, and Jarābodhīya [Sāmans]. *Ayā pavasva pavate* consists of the Sapha and Akṣāra [Sāmans] for the two single verses.

"pra sunvānaḥ" is the Gaurīvita [sāman] on one verse; the Vaiśvāmitrapadanidhana, Śuddhāśuddhīya, Svāra, Kautsa, Sādhu, Ākūpāra, Gautama, and Kāva as the final [sāman]. Everything else is like the first day. All [the stotras] consist of thirty-three verses.

For the second day: *pavasva vācaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā soma vṛṣā hy asi*, and this ten-verse hymn beginning with *eṣa devaḥ*; the eight-verse hymn beginning with *eṣa dhiyā*; and for the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant, the verses beginning with *pavamānasya te vayam*. At the midday pressing, the *gāyatra*, *yukta-aśva*, *surūpa*, and *hariśrī-nidhana* [stotras] are performed with the verses beginning with *vṛṣā pavasva*. For the *mādhyaṃdina-pavamāna*, the *samanta-dairghaśravasa*, *pṛṣṭha-kaulmalabarhiṣa*, *aiḍa-māyāsya*, and *triṇidhana-māyāsya* [stotras] are performed with the verses beginning with *punānaḥ soma*. The final [stotra] is the *vāsiṣṭha* with the verse beginning with *vṛṣā śoṇaḥ*. All [these stotras] consist of three-verse units (*tṛca*).

In the Ārbhava [Śastra], the stotras are: "yaste madaḥ" with the *gāyatra*, *haviṣmat*, *śaṃmada*, and *avasunidhana* [dhurs]; "pavasvendraṃ accha" with the *śaṅku* and *sujñāna* [dhurs]; and "ayaṃ pūṣā" with the *gaurīvita*, *aiḍa*, *autsa*, *śyāvāśva*, and *garga* [dhurs]. "vṛṣā matīnām" is the final [stotra] of the Yāma. All [these stotras] consist of three verses (*tṛca*). Everything else is like the second day. Everything is [performed] with the thirty-three-fold hymn.

For the third day: *ete rājā* (RV 9.61.1–5), *tantvānṛmṇāni* (RV 9.61.20–24)—these two form a five-verse hymn; *asṛgran* (RV 9.62.1–9) is a nine-verse hymn; *yavaṃ-yava* (RV 9.65.1–4) is a four-verse hymn; and *apaghnanniṣe pavasva* (RV 9.66.1–20) constitutes the Bahiṣpavamāna stotra. At the midday pressing: *uccā ta* (RV 8.69.1–3) consists of the Gāyatra, Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha, Saumitra, and Aiṭata sūktas. *abhi soma* (RV 9.107.1–21) consists of the Paurumadga, Sadoviśīya, Gautama, Antarikṣa, Mādhātitha, Āṣkāraṇidhana, and Kāṇva sūktas. *tisro vācaḥ* (RV 8.61.1–17) has the Aṅgirasām-krośa as its final part. All [of these] consist of triplets (*tṛca*).

In the *ārbhava* [laud], there are three [stotras]: the *gāyatra*, the *pāṣṭhaudha*, the *aiḍa*, and the *saindhukṣita*; and the *vācaḥsāman* and the *śaukta* with "āsotā sakhāya" as their [starting] verses; and the *gaurīvita*, the *sādhrasvāra*, the *tvāṣṭrīsāman*, the *triṇidhana*, the *tvāṣṭrīsāman* with repetition, and the *tvāṣṭrīsāman* with repetition; and the *ariṣṭa* with "pavitrante" as its final [verse]. All are triplets (*tṛca*). Everything else is like the third day. Everything is [based on] the thirty-threefold [Stoma].

For the fourth day: *pra ta ajījanat*, *prayadgāḥ*—these two six-versed hymns; *āśuṣṣaḍṛcam*; *babhruṣṣaḍṛcam*; *prasvā navarcam*; and *hinvanti* as the Bahiṣpavamāna. From *prasvā navarce*, one should omit the final triplet. At the midday pressing: *pavasva dakṣa* with the Gāyatra, Atharvaṇa, Nidhana, Kāma, and Adārasṛj chants; *tavāhaṃ soma* with the Āśadaṃṣṭra, Uttarārka, Puṣpa, and others, including the Bārhaduktha, Māṇḍava, Abhīśava, Adivasvaḥpṛṣṭha, and Āṅgirasa hymns.

"Punānaḥ" is the final [verse] of the Satrāsāhīya; all [the following] are triplets (tṛca). In the Ārbhava [laud], "pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" consists of the Gāyatra, Ūrṇīyava, Bṛhat, Bhāradvāja-nidhana, Mārgīyava, and Āṇi [stotras]. "Tvaṃ hy aṅga daivya somaḥ punānaḥ" consists of the Bṛhat and Kātīṣādīya [stotras]. "Purojitī" consists of the Nānada, Eḍa-śuddha-aśuddhīya, Ākūpāra, and Andhīgava [stotras]. "Somaḥ pavate" is the final Vātsapra. All are triplets. Everything else is like the fourth day. All [the stotras] consist of thirty-three [verses], as does the Ṣoḍaśin-sāman.

For the fifth day: *govit*, *viśvavit*, *dadhanniṣu*, and the seven-verse hymn; *prakaviḥ* and the seven-verse hymn; *yavaṃ-yava* and the four-verse hymn; *ayāvī*, *atipaghnanyāste dhāraḥ*—these constitute the *bahiṣpavamāna*. At the midday pressing: *arṣā soma* and so forth, including the *gāyatra*, *ṇva*, *śākala*, and *vārṣa* hymns; *soma uṣva* and so forth, including the *mānava*, *anūpa*, *vaiṣṇava*, *ādyayukta*, *sruc*, *vāma*, and *agni-triṇidhana* hymns; *yatsoma citram* and so forth, including the *śaiśava* as the final one. All [these] consist of triplets (*tṛca*).

In the Ārbhava [Śastra], the verses beginning with "asāvyaṃśuḥ" form the Gāyatra-saṃtani; there are two and a half *iḍā*s, and the Soma-sāmans are sung upon the *gūktāni* (the hymns). Everything else is like the fifth day; everything consists of thirty-three [verses].
The sixth day is according to the archetype.

The Sixth Chapter: The Variations of the Twelve-Day Rite; the Seventh Day—*prakāprasvānavarcam*, *asṛgrannavarcam*, *prayadgāṣaḍṛcam*, *yavaṃyavaṃ caturṛcam*. The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant begins with *ā te dakṣam*; there is an omission (*uddhāra*) of the final verse of the four-verse hymn. At the midday pressing, for the *gāyatrasantani* [stoma], there are the *aiḍa*, *sauparṇa*, *rohitakūlīya*, *gauṣūkta*, and *śākala* chants. For the *paurumadga*, *kaṇvarathantara*, *gauṅgava*, *vinidhana*, and *māyāsya* chants, [the verses] begin with *punānaḥ soma*. The *pravad-bhārgava* chant, ending with *pro āyāsīt*, is the final one.

All [the verses] consist of triplets (*tṛca*). In the *ārbhava* [stotra], after the *kārtayaśa*, one should insert the *svāra* [chanting] and the *nidhana* of the *tvāṣṭrīsāman*, as well as the *gautama* [chants]. Everything [should be performed] with the *trayastriṃśa* [stoma].

For the eighth day: *śiśum ete somābhīnavarcam*, *somaḥ punānonavarcam*, *somā asṛgrannavarcam*, and *ayā pavasva dhārayā* for the Bahiṣpavamāna. At the midday pressing: *adhvaryo adribhissutam* for the Gāyatra, Vairūpa, Āśubha, Bhārgava, Mārgīyava, Saumitra, Sākamaśva, Vilamba, and Sauparṇa [stotras]. *Abhi somāsa āyayuḥ* for the Dvihiṅkāra, Vāmadevya, Gāyatra, Pārśva, and Pauruhanmana [stotras]. *Dhartā divaḥ* for the Udvat-Bhārgava at the end.

"O God, flow for the Ārbhava [laud], for life"—these are the Gāyatra, Svāśira, and Ārkagāyatra Sāmans. "Toward glory, the breath, the infant"—these are the Aiṣira and Atrāta. "Toward us, the most excellent winner of booty"—these are the Gaurīvita, Aiḍa, Kautsa, Audala, and Rayiṣṭha Sāmans in their own Dharmas. "They urge on"—this is the Viśoviśīya at the end. Everything else is like the eighth day; everything is Trayastrimśa.

For the ninth day: *akrāna eṣa devaḥ* is a ten-verse hymn; *eṣa u ṣaḍṛcam* is a six-verse hymn; *eṣa vājī* is a six-verse hymn; *eṣa kaviḥ* is a six-verse hymn. For the *bahiṣpavamāna*, the verse is *pavamānasya te kavaḥ*; in the ten-verse hymn, the final verse is omitted. At the midday pressing, for the *pṛṣṭha-stotra*, there are the *gāyatra*, *ādārasṛj*, *iḍānāṃsaṃkṣāra*, and *ṛṣabhapavamāna* chants. For the *pṛṣṭha-stotra* on three verses, the chant is *parīto ṣi*. The triplets of Sāmans are those of Kaulmalabarhiṣa, Arkapuṣpa, and Dairghaśravasa.

The *devasthāna*, *saṃskṛti*, *vaiyaśva*, *abhīśava*, and the *uttara* [stotras] are performed upon triplets (*tṛcas*). The final hymn (*arka*) of Dīrghatamas begins with "asāvi soma. Or else, the *sāmarāja* is used. In the latter view regarding the *sāmarāja*, at the midday pressing, in place of the *pṛṣṭha-stotra*, there are the *pṛṣṭha-dīrghatama-arka-māṇḍava* triplet-sāmans. At the third pressing (*ārbhava*), the *gāyatra* beginning with "tvā soma" is chanted over three verses. The *aśvasūkta-pratīcīna*, *iḍāṅka*, and *āśītahāviṣkṛta* [are also included]. The *sauparṇa* and *vaiśvamanasa* are the single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*) beginning with "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya" and "pavasva daivavītaye," respectively.

"Pari tyam" (RV 1.84), "Gaurīvita," and "Ekasyām"; "Nihavayad-vāhiṣṭhīya," "Asitāt," and "Sādhrāṇi"; "Vidharma" in its own [verses]; "Upoṣu" as the final "Śrudhya"—all this is like the ninth [day] with an *āhava*. All [these] consist of thirty-three [verses].

For the tenth day: *asṛkṣata pra vājinaḥ*, *pavamānasya viśvavit*, *pavamāno ajījanat*, *ete asṛgram indavaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā sutaḥ*, and *somaḥ punānaḥ*—these constitute nine verses for the *bahiṣpavamāna*. [The sequence is: *asya pratnām anu dyutam*, *anu pratnāsa āyavaḥ*, and so forth, up to the end of the *bahiṣpavamāna*. At the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*), there are the *uccā te gāyatra*, *āmahīyava*, *ājīga*, and *abhīkā* chants; the *punānaḥ soma* chant; the *raurava*, *yaudhājaya*, *dairghaśravasa*, *utsedha*, and *yajñāyajñīya-niṣedha* chants; and the *gaurīvita* chant ending with *ājāgri viḥ*.

All [the stotras] consist of triplets (*tṛca*). In the Ārbhava [Pavamāna], there are the Gāyatra, Saṃhitaka, Kākṣīvata, Bhāsaja, and Jarābodhīya [stotras] with the verse *svādiṣṭhayā*. There are the Sapha and Rohitakūlīya with the verse *pavasvendram accha*. There are the Śyāvāśva and Āndhīgava with the verse *pary ū ṣu*. There is the Sauhaviṣa with the verse *pari pra dhanva*. The final [stotra] is the Vājajit among those beginning with *sūryavatīṣu*. All are triplets. Everything else is like the tenth day. Everything is [performed] on the thirty-third day. The rules for the tenth day are to be carried out with a common procedure (*samānasā*).
[The forty-fold-stoma twelve-day rite is the seventh.
Now he describes the forty-fold-stoma twelve-day rite,
as in the case of the seventh.
He states the qualified person: "Therefore, one who desires splendor or one who desires Vedic luster [should perform it]."

Thus [it is said]. The word "one should sacrifice" (yajeta) is understood to carry over. Its ritual arrangement (klṛpti) is like that of the Aṅgirasa-ayanana, the Chandoma, and the Daśarātra: additions (āvāpa) and omissions (udvāpa) should be performed in accordance with the *stomas*.

Regarding the first day: for the *bahiṣpavamāna*, [the verses] are "asya pratnānu," "ete somā abhi," "agna āyūṃṣi," and "pavamānasya te kava. At the midday pressing, [the stotras] are the Gāyatra, Aśva, Soma, Sāman, and Āśubhārgava, beginning with "pra somāso vipaścitaḥ"; the Pajra, Gauṅgava, and Audhājaya, beginning with "pra soma devavītaye"; and the Auśana as the final one. At the third pressing (*ārbhava*), [the stotras] are the Gāyatra and Saṃhita, beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā"; and the Sapha and Akṣāra, beginning with "pavasvendramaccha."

The *pra sunvānaḥ* hymns, the *gaurīvitagautama-padanidhana*, the *śuddha-śuddhīya* hymns, and the *kāva* as the final [hymn]—all these consist of triplets (*tṛca*). Everything else is like the first day [of the *pr̥ṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*]. The entire twenty-fourth day is like this arrangement of the first day of the ten-night period of the *Chandoma* within the *Aṅgirasām ayana*.

For the second day: *pavasva vācaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā soma*, and *vṛṣā hy asya eṣa u*—this is the six-verse [stotra]. For the *bahiṣpavamāna*: *ayā pavasva*, *pavamānasya te vayam*. At the midday [pressing], for the *gāyatrau ktāśva* [chant]: *vṛṣā pavasva*. For the *pṛṣṭhya-śas*: the *kaulmalabarhiṣa*, the *aiḍa*, the *māyāsya*, the *triṇidhana*, and the *māyāsya* chants. For the final [stotra]: the *vāsiṣṭha* beginning with *vṛṣā śoṇaḥ*. At the *ārbhava* [pressing]: the *gāyatrahāviṣmat* beginning with *yaste madaḥ*.

"Pavasva indram accha" is for the Śaṅkusujñāna; "Ayaṃ pūṣā" consists of the Gaurīvita, Bharga, and the three following Krauñca verses; "Vṛṣā matīnām" is the final Yāma hymn. All [these] are triplets (tṛcas). Everything else is like the second day. And everything is the Caturviṃśa [Stoma].

For the third day: *davi ete rājā tantvānṛpaḥ* is a hymn of eight verses; *eṣa dhiyā* is a hymn of eight verses; *iṣe pavasva dhārayā* is the Bahiṣpavamāna stotra. In the hymn of eight verses, the last verse is omitted. At the midday pressing: *uccā ta* consists of the Gāyatra, Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha, Saumitra, Abhisoma (Paurumadga), Gautama, Antarikṣa, Āṣkāraṇidhana, and Kāṇva [hymns]. *tisro vācaḥ* is the final Aṅgirasām-saṃkrośa. All [these] consist of triplets.

In the *ārbhava* [laud], there are three [verses] beginning with "vācaḥ" in the *gāyatrapāṣṭhaudha*; "āsotā—sakhāyaḥ" in the *vācaḥsāmaśaukta*; "sutāso me" in the *gaurīvitaiḍatvāṣṭrīsāma*, *triṇidhanatvāṣṭrīsāma*, and [others]; and "pavitraṃ te" as the final [verse], which is the *ariṣṭa*. All [these] are triplets (*tṛca*). Everything else is like the third day. And all [this] is the *caturviṃśa* [stoma].

For the fourth day: *pra te ajījanat* (the first triplet), *prayadgāḥ*, *āśuṣṣaḍṛcam*, *babhruṣṣaḍṛce*—these are the initial triplets; the *bahiṣpavamāna* chant begins with *hinvanti*. At the midday pressing, the chants beginning with *pavasva dakṣa* have the *gāyatra*, *ātharvaṇa*, *nidhana*, and *kāma* melodies. The chants beginning with *tavāhaṃ soma* include the *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*, *uttarārka*, *puṣpa*, *abhīśu*, *ādya*, *svaḥpṛṣṭha*, and *āṅgirasa* melodies. The final chant is *punānaḥ satrāsāhīyam*. All [of these] consist of triplets (*tṛca*).

In the Ārbhava [Śastra], the verses beginning with "pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" are in the Gāyatrī meter; these are the Ūrṇāyava, Bṛhat, and Bhāradvāja [Sāmans]. "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā" is the Bṛhat from the Kātīṣādīya [collection]. "purojitī" is the Nānada and the Andhīgava [Sāmans]. "somaḥ pavate" is the Vātsapra at the end. All [these] consist of triplets (tṛcas). Everything else is like the fourth day [of the Pr̥ṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha]. The entire [rite] is the Caturviṃśa; and so is the Ṣoḍaśin Sāman.

For the fifth day: *govit*, *viśvavit*, *adhanviṣuḥ*—these constitute the seven-verse [stotra]. *Pra kaviḥ*—this is the seven-verse [stotra]. *Yavaṃ yavam*—this is the four-verse [stotra]. *Yāste* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. From the seven-verse *pra kaviḥ*, one should exclude the final triplet. At the midday [pressing]: *arṣā soma* consists of the *gāyatra*, *anvaśākala*, and *vārṣa* [hymns]. *Soma u ṣvā* consists of the *mānava*, *ānūpa*, and *āgneyatriṇidhana* [hymns]. *Yat soma citram* is the *śaiśava*; this is the final [hymn]. All [these] are triplets.

In the *ārbhava* [laud], "asāvyaṃśuḥ" is the *gāyatra-santani*; "abhi dyumnam prāṇāḥ śiśuḥ" is the *cyāvana-krośa*; and "pavasva vājasātaye" are the *gaurīvitā*, *āśvatrāsadasyavā*, *aṣṭeḍa*, and *padastobha* [stotriyas] in the triplets (*tṛcas*). "Indur vājī" is the final [verse] of the *dāśaspatya*. All [these] are triplets. Everything else is like the fifth day; everything is the *caturviṃśa* [stoma].

The Sixth Chapter: Variations of the Twelve-Day Rite; the Sixth Day—*Jyotis*, *Asṛk*, *Vīrat*, and the ten-verse hymn; *Sanāca* and *Soma*, each a single verse; *Taratsama*, four verses; *Ete Soma*, for the *Bahiṣpavamāna*. At the midday [pressing], *Indrāyendu*, *Gāyatreṣovṛdhīya*, and *Revatī* verses; *Mṛjyamāna*, the *Svāra*, *Auksnorandhra*, *Vājajit*, *Varuṇasāma*, and *Goṣṭha*; *Etamu tyam*, the *Ihavat-vāmadevya*, as the final [hymn]. All [these] consist of triplets (*tṛca*). At the third pressing (*ārbhava*), *Parisvāna*, the *Gāyatra*, *Tṛtīyavat*, and *Vaidanvata*.

The *sakhyam* [stotra] begins with "sa sutam vaḥ sakhe" for one who desires long-lasting fame; the *gaurīvita*, *madhuścunnidhana*, and *aiḍakrauñca* [stotras] are performed with the verses beginning "somāḥ pavante"; the *śnauṣṭa* [stotra] has "ayā pavasva pavasva" as its final verse. All [these stotras] consist of triplets (*tṛca*). Everything else is like that of the sixth day. And everything is according to the *caturviṃśa* [rite].
The sixth day is according to the archetype.

For the eighth day: "These Somas for the Child" (*śiśum ete somābhinavaḥ*) with nine verses; "Soma purifying himself" (*somaḥ punānonavaḥ*) with nine verses; and "Flow on with this stream" (*ayā pavasva dhārayā*) as the *bahiṣpavamāna*. At the midday pressing: "O Adhvaryu, [the Soma] pressed with stones" (*adhvaryo adribhiḥ sutam*) consists of the *gāyatra*, *vairūpa*, *āśabha*, *ārgava*, and *mārgīyava* chants. "Toward the Soma" (*abhi soma*) consists of the *dvihiṃkāra*, *vāmadevya*, *gāyatra*, *pārśva*, and *pauruhanmana* chants. "The upholder of heaven" (*dhartā divaḥ*) consists of the *udvat* and the final *bhārgava*. All [these] are triplets (*tṛca*). At the third pressing: "Flow on, O God, for life" (*pavasva deva āyuṣak*) is the *gāyatra* sung over three verses.

The *sāman*-verses are *svāśira*, *arka*, *kākṣīvata*, and *bhāsā*. "Abhi dyumnam," "prāṇāḥ," and "śiśuḥ"—these are the *aiṣira* verses here. "Abhī no vājasātamam" is the *gaurīvitaiḍa-kautsa*; its own [verses] are the *dharma*. "Hinvanti" is the final verse of the *viśoviśīya*. All are triplets (*tṛca*). Everything else is like the eighth day. And everything is like the Caturviṃśa day.

For the ninth day: *akrān eṣa devaḥ* is the ten-verse hymn; *eṣa dhiyā* is the eight-verse hymn; *pavamānasya te kavaḥ* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. At the midday pressing, *pavamānasya jighnataḥ* constitutes the *gāyatradāraruṅṛṣabhapavamānas*. *parīto ṣi* contains the *pṛṣṭhasaṃkṛti*, *dairghaśravasa*, and *devasthāna* [stotras] upon triplets. *asāvi somaḥ* is the final *arka* of Dīrghatamas; or else, the *sāmarāja*. In the latter case, where the *sāmarāja* is final, it takes the place of the *pṛṣṭha*.

The *pṛṣṭha* [stotras] consist of the *dīrghatamas*, *arka*, *māṇḍava*, and *sāmatṛca* hymns. In the *ārbhava* [stotra], there is the *gāyatra* chant on three verses beginning with "tvaṃ soma. There are the *āśvasūkta*, *pratīcīna*, *aiḍa*, *kāśīta*, and *hāviṣmat* chants, each consisting of three verses. The *sauparṇa* and *vaiśvamanasa* chants are "tvaṃ hyaṅga" and "daivyapavasva devavītaye. The *gaurīvita* chant is "pari tyam" on two verses. The *dharma* chant is performed on its own verses. The *śrudhya* chant is "upoṣu jātam," which is the final one. All these are triplets (*tṛca*). Everything else is like the ninth day. And everything is like the *caturviṃśa* day.
The tenth day is according to the archetype; the Agniṣṭoma is also the Caturviṃśa.
[The forty-fourth-stoma twelve-day rite is the eighth:
He speaks of the forty-fourth-stoma twelve-day rite—
just as the eighth.
Thus; it is to be explained as before. || 16 ||
He states the qualified person: "By that [rite], one who desires splendor or one who desires vigor [should perform it]. (17)

Thus [it is said]. The word "one should sacrifice" (yajeta) is understood to carry over. Its arrangement is like that of the Ādityānām ayana and the Chandoma-daśarātra; additions and omissions (āvāpa-udvāpa) should be made in accordance with the *stomas*.

Regarding the first day: *asya pratnānavarcam*, *ete somābhīnavarcam*, *somaḥ punāno navarcam*, *somā asṛgrannavarcam*, *pavasvavṛpañcarcam*, and *pavamānasya te kavaḥ* constitute the Bahiṣpavamāna. At the midday [pressing], *pra somāso vipaścitaḥ* constitutes the Gāyatra, Aśva, Soma, Sāman, Āśubha, Bhārgava, Mārgīyava, Abhīka, Aiḍasa, Suparṇa, and Rohitakūlīya. *Pra soma devavītaye* is the Pajra on a single verse; on that same verse is the Dvaigata.

The *pauruhanmana*, *hārāyaṇa*, *dvihiṃkāra*, *vāmadevya*, *gauṅgava*, *audhājaya*, and the last one, *auśana*; in the *ārbhava* [laud], the *gāyatra*, *saṃhita*, *kākṣīvata*, *bhāsa*, *śaiśava*, *jarābodhīya*, and the two single-verse hymns beginning with "pavasva indram accha" and "saphākṣāre";
the sixth chapter—variations of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*):

the *gaurīvitavaiśvāmitra*, *padanidhana*, *śuddhāśudvīya*, *svāra*, *kautsa*, *aurukṣaya*, *audala*, and *gautama*; the *kāva* is the last; everything else is like the first day; all [stomas] are the forty-four-fold (*catuścatvāriṃśa*).

For the second day: *pavasva vācaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā soma*, *vṛṣā hyasi*, *eṣa deva*—these are the ten-verse [stotras]. *Eṣa u ṣaḍṛcam*, *eṣa vājī ṣaḍṛcam*, *eṣa kaviḥ*—these are the six-verse [stotras]. *Utte śuṣmāso asthuḥ* is the four-verse [stotra]. *Pavamānasya te vayam* is the Bahiṣpavamāna. From the ten-verse [stotra], one should omit the final triplet.

At the midday pressing, [the stotras] are: *vṛṣā pavasva* with the *gāyatra*, *yukta-aśva*, *surūpa*, *hari-śrī*, *nidhana*, *ajiga*, *svāra*, *sauparṇa*, *yukta-aśva*, *ṛṣabha*, and *pavamāna* chants; *punānaḥ soma* with the *samanta*, *dairghaśravasa*, and the first [chant]; the *pṛṣṭhya*, *yaśas*, *kaulmalabarhiṣa*, *aiḍa*, *māyāsya*, *triṇidhana*, and *māyāsya* chants; *vṛṣā śoṇaḥ* as the final [chant] belonging to Vasiṣṭha; and at the third pressing (*ārbhava*), *yas te madaḥ* with the *gāyatra*, *hāviṣmat*, *śāmmada*, *dāvasu-nidhana*, *adhyardheḍa*, *soma-sāman*, and *aśva-sūkta* chants.

"Flow forth with this stream for the feast of the gods"—these two single-verse hymns are for the *śaṅkusujñāna* [stoma]; or alternatively, "Flow forth toward Indra"—this is for the *śaṅkusujñāna*. "This one, O Pūṣan"—the *gaurīvita*, *aiḍa*, *kaunsa*, *bharga*, *asitayadvāhiṣṭhīya*, *krauñca*, and those beginning with the *akrauñca* follow. "The bull of prayers"—this is the final *yāma*. Everything else is like the second day. All [stomas] are the forty-four-fold (*catuścatvāriṃśa*).

For the third day: *davadyete rājā*, *tantvānṛmṇāni*—these five verses; *eṣa dhiyā*—eight verses; *asṛgran*—nine verses; *pavamānā asṛkṣata*, *apaghnan*, *pra te dhārāḥ*—four verses; *iṣa*—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna. At the midday pressing: *uccā te*—the Gāyatra, Kṣullakavaiṣṭambha, Saumitra, Aiṭata, Sākamaśva, Vilamba, Sauparṇa, and Abhīka hymns; *abhi somena*—the Paurumadga hymn in the first [turn].

The *sadoviśīya*, *raurava*, *ubhayatastobha*, *gautama*, *antarikṣa*, *acchidra*, *medhātithi*, the *āṣkāraṇidhana*, the *madhyāsyāya*, and the final *saṃkrośa* of the Aṅgirases beginning with "tisro vācaḥ. In the Ārbhava Pavamāna, there are the *gāyatrapāṣṭha*, *auhaiḍa*, *saindhukṣita*, *agnerarka*, and *auśanasa-saṃhita* hymns beginning with "tisro vāca udīrate. Then follow the *vācaḥsāman* and *śaukta* for the two single-verse hymns beginning with "ā sotā sakhāyaḥ."

The *sāmans* are: "sutāso me" (Gaurīvita), "sādhra" (Śyāvāśva), "aiḍaṃ tvāṣṭrīsāma", "svāraṃ tvāṣṭrīsāma", "triṇidhanaṃ tvāṣṭrīsāma", and "abhyāsaṃ tvāṣṭrīsāma". "pavitraṃ te" is the final [verse], which is the *ariṣṭa*. Everything else is like the third day; all [verses] consist of forty syllables.

For the fourth day: *pra ta ajījanat* (six verses), *prayadgāḥ* (six verses), *āśuṣṣaḍṛcam*, *babhruḥṣaḍṛcam*, *prasvānavarcam*, and *eṣa dhiyā* (eight verses). The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant begins with *hinvanti*. At the midday pressing, the *ādrasṛcaḥ* (verses for the desire of the Gāyatra-Ātharvaṇa *nidhana*) begin with *pavasva dakṣa*. In the first verse of the sequence beginning with *tavāha soma*, *āṣṭādaṃṣṭra*, *uttarārka*, and *puṣpa*.

The *pauruhanmana*, *dvaigata*, *gauṅgava*, *bārhaduktha*, *māṇḍava*, *samanta*, *yaudhājaya*, *abhīśava*, *svaḥpṛṣṭha*, and *āṅgirasa* [stotras]; "punānaḥ" is the *satrāsāhīya*, which is the last [verse]. In the *ārbhava* [stotra], "pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ" consists of the *gāyatra*, *aurṇāyava*, *bṛhat*, *bhāradvāja*, and *mārgīyava* [verses]. "tvaṃ hyaṅga daivya somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā" consists of the *vṛhat* and *kātīṣādīya*, which are two single-verse [hymns].

The *nānadeḍa*, *śuddhāśuddhīya*, *andhīgava*, *vaitahavya*, *somasāman*, *krauñca*, and so forth, the *madhuścunnidhana*, *ākūpāra*, *bṛhat*, and *āgneya* [are the *ṣoḍaśin* chants]. The *vātsapra* ending with "Soma pavate" is the final one. Everything else is like the fourth day. Everything is the forty-four-fold [stoma], as is the *ṣoḍaśi-sāman*.

For the fifth day: *govid*, *viśvajit*, and *adhanviṣu*—these constitute a hymn of seven verses (*saptarca*). *Pra kaviḥ*—a hymn of seven verses. *Yavaṃ yavam*—a hymn of four verses. *Somā asṛgran*—a hymn of nine verses. *Utte śu*—a hymn of five verses. *Ayāvītiyāste dhāraḥ* is the *bahiṣpavamāna*. At the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*), *arṣā soma* and so forth are the *gāyatrasaṃtanī* verses, consisting of the *iṇva*, *śākala*, *vārśa*, *vārṣāhara*, and *āpatya* hymns. *Soma u ṣvā* and so forth are the *vaiṣṇava* and subsequent *vaiṣṇava* verses, beginning with the first.

The *mānavottara*, *anūpavāman*, *vāmra*, *yauktasruk*, *hārāyaṇa*, *agni*, and *triṇidhana* [are the stotras]; the *sāman* "yat sāma citram" is the final *śaiśava*. In the *ārbhava* [laud], there are the *gāyatra*, *adhyardha*, *iḍaṃsa*, *somasāman*, *goṣūkta*, *iḍaṃsa*, and *aindhukṣita*.
The sixth [section] concerns the variations of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*).

The two single-verse hymns at the *cyāvana* and *krośa* [stomas] are "Abhi dyumnam" and "Prāṇā śiśuḥ. The verses beginning with "Pavasva vājasātaye" belong to Gaurīvita, Ṛṣabha, Śākvara, Ātreya, Rayiṣṭha, Pārtha, Aśvatrāsadasyava, Andhīgava, Śyāvāśva, Aṣṭeḍa, Pada, and Stobha. "Indur vājī" belongs to Dāśaspati. Everything else is like the fifth day; everything is in the forty-four-fold (*catuścatvāriṃśa*) stoma.

For the sixth day: *Jyotir asṛkṣata* (ten verses); *Sanād divaḥ* (ten verses); *Taratsamandī* (four verses); *Eṣa kaviḥ* (six verses); *Sasutaḥ* (six verses); and *Ete soma* for the *bahiṣpavamāna*. In the *sasutaḥ* hymn of six verses, the last verse is omitted. For the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*), there are the *gāyatras*, the *aiṣovṛdhīya*, the *krauñca*, the *dārḍhyacyuta*, the *vājadāvarya*, the *raivata*, and the *aśvasūkta* beginning with *Indrāyendavo*. In the verse beginning *Mṛjyamānaḥ*, there is the *aiḍa*, the *aukṣṇorandhra-svāra*, and the *aukṣṇorandhra* melody on the first verse.

The *samanta*, *vājajit*, *varuṇasāman*, *arkapuṣpa*, *uttaragoṣṭha*, *triṇidhana*, *māyāsyāni*, and the *vāmadevya* [sāman] beginning with "etamu tyam" and ending with "ihavat"; in the *ārbhava* [stotra], the *parisvāna*, the *gāyatra*, the third *vaivanvata*, the first *vaivanvata*, the fourth *vaivanvata*, the *hāviṣmat*, the *haivat*, the *aidhmavāha*, the *pratīcīna-ḍaṅkāśīta-payāṃsi*; and for the two single verses, [the hymns] beginning with "sa sutaṃ vaḥ sakha" for Dīrghakārṇaśravas.

The *somaḥ pavante* [stotra] consists of the *gaurīvita*, the *madhuścunnidhana*, the *dhīgava*, the *vāṅnidhana*, the *krauñca*, and the *aiḍakrauñca*. The final [stotra] is the *śnauṣṭa* with the verse *ayā pavā pavasva*. Everything else is like the sixth day. Everything is in the forty-four-fold [tune].

On the seventh day: *prakā-prasvāna* consisting of nine verses; *asṛgram* consisting of nine verses; *prayadgāḥ* consisting of six verses; *āśuḥ* consisting of six verses; *eṣa dhiyā* consisting of eight verses; and for the *bahiṣpavamāna*, *ā te dakṣam*. At the midday pressing, for the *gāyatrasaṃtanī*, there are the *aiḍa*, *sauparṇa*, *rohitakūlīya*, *goṣūkta*, *śākala*, and *ājiga* hymns. For the *gauṅgava* and *paurumadga* [stotras], the verse "punānaḥ soma" is used in the first [turn].

The *Kaṇvarathantara*, the *Soma-sāman* with the *dvini-dhana*, the *Āyāsya-aiḍa*, the *Āyāsya-vārṣabha*, the *Bhāradvāja-pṛśni*, and the *pro ayāsīt*—this last being the final *pravat* of the *Bhārgava* [family]. In the *ārbhava* [stotra], there are the *Gāyatra* of Agni, the *arka*, the *adhyardheḍa*, the *Soma-sāman*, and the *aukṣa* [verses]. The *eṣa sya dhārayā sakhā* are the *Śārkaraplava* [sāmans] on two single verses (*ekarca*). The *purojitī* [verse] contains the *Gaurīvita*, the *Kārtayaśa*, the *Kṣullaka-kāleya*, the *Svāra-tvaṣṭrīsāman*, the *Nidhana-tvaṣṭrīsāman*, the *Andhīgava*, the *Krauñca*, and the *Agra-gautama*.
"pra vājyakṣeti" is the *sauhaviṣa*; "ye someti" is the final *jarābodhīya*. Everything else is like that of the seventh day. Everything is the forty-four-fold [stoma].
The eighth day is according to the archetype.

Regarding the ninth day: in the *bahiṣpavamāna*, one should extract the four subsequent verses from the eight-verse hymn beginning with "eṣa dhiyā. In the midday pressing, one should extract [the verses] for the *iḍā* and the *saṃkṣāra-dairghaśravasa*. In the third pressing, one should extract the single verses for the *svāra-sauparṇa* and the *vaiśvamanasa*. Everything else is like the ninth day; everything is in the forty-four-fold stoma.

For the tenth day: *asṛkṣata pravājinaḥ*, *pavamānasya viśvavit*, *pavamāno dhajījanat*, *ete asṛgram indavaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā sutaḥ*, *dhanviṣuḥ*—these constitute the seven-versed [stotras]. *pra kaviḥ*—the seven-versed [stotra]. *babhruḥ*—the six-versed [stotra]. *asya pratnāmanvarcaḥ*—this forms the Bahiṣpavamāna. At the midday [pressing], there are the Gāyatra, Āmahīyava, Ājīgarta, Bhīka, Gauṣūkta, Satrāsāhīya, and Vairūpa [sāmans] beginning with *uccā te*.

In the *raurava* and *yaudhājaya* [stotras], the first [verse] is "punaḥ soma. There follow the *ubhayataḥstobha*, *gautama*, *mahāvaiṣṭambha*, *gauṅgava*, *utsedha*, *yajñāyajñīya*, and *niṣedha*. The last is the *gaurīvitam* with "ājāgri viri. In the *ārbhava* [stotra], there are the *svādiṣṭhayā*, *gāyatra*, *saṃhita*, *jarābodhīya*, *kṣullakavaiṣṭambha*, *śaiśava*, *maukṣaka*, *ākṣīvata*, *bhāsa*, *aiḍaka*, *autsa*, and the *agnir arkāḥ*. In the two single-verse [stotras], there are the *sapha* and *rohitakūlīya* with "pavasva indram accha. The *śyāvāśva* and *āndhīgava* are with "pary ū ṣu. "Pari pradhanva" is the sixth chapter—the options for the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*).

The *sauhaviṣa* [is as follows]: that which ends with "of the Sun" (*sūryasya*) is the *vājajit*; everything else is like the tenth day. Everything is forty-four-fold. The duties of the tenth day are to be performed with the same *sāman*. ||17||
[The forty-eight-fold-stoma twelve-day rite is the ninth.
He speaks of the forty-eight-fold-stoma twelve-day rite—
just as the ninth.
Thus; it is to be explained as before. ||||
He states the qualified person: "By that [rite], one who desires consecration or one who desires offspring."

Thus [it is said]. The word "one should sacrifice" (*yajeta*) is understood from the context. Its ritual arrangement (*klṛpti*) should be performed like that of the twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*) with the forty-four-fold hymn-form (*catuścatvāriṃśastoma*).

For the first day: in the *bahiṣpavamāna*, one should place the four-verse hymn (*caturṛca*) "pra te dhārāḥ" before the *paryāsa* hymn "pavamānasya te kave". In the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*), the three-verse hymns (*tṛca*) are formed from the *pajra* and *dvigata* chants. In the third pressing (*ārbhava*), the three-verse hymns are formed from the *sapha* and *pauṣkala* chants. The specific distinction is that everything consists of the forty-eight-fold hymn-form (*aṣṭācatvāriṃśa*).

For the second day: *pavasva vācaḥ*, *pavasvendo vṛṣā soma*, and *vṛṣā hyasi*—this is the ten-verse [hymn] for the deity; this is the six-verse [hymn] for Uṣas; this is the six-verse [hymn] for Vājin; this is the six-verse [hymn] for Kavi; and *ut te śuṣmaḥ* is the five-verse [hymn]. "O Pavamāna, of thee, the sage" (*pavamānasya te kave*) constitutes the Bahiṣpavamāna chant. For both the Mādhyandina and Ārbhava pavamānas, the procedure consists entirely of forming triplets (*tṛca*). The specific distinction is that everything totals forty-eight verses.

On the third day, during the *bahiṣpavamāna*, one should place a four-verse hymn beginning with "For food, flow pure" (*iṣe pavasva*) before the *paryāsa* chant, inserting it verse by verse. For both the midday and the third pressings, all [stotras] are formed into triplets; the specific distinction is that everything consists of forty-eight verses.

On the fourth day: before the *paryāsa* of the *bahiṣpavamāna*, one should place the four-verse hymn beginning with "hinvanti" after [the verse] "utte śuṣmāso asthuḥ. For both the midday and the third *pavamāna* lauds, all [stotras] are formed into triplets (*tṛca*). Everything consists of forty-eight verses, including the *ṣoḍaśin* chant; this is the specific rule.

On the fifth day: in the *bahiṣpavamāna*, before the *paryāsa* [stotra], one should place the four-verse hymn beginning with "pra te dhārāḥ" after the verse beginning with "yāste dhārāḥ. At the midday pressing, on the *bṛhatī* verses, the *sāman*-triplets are those beginning with the Vaiṣṇava, the Uttaramānava, and the Ādyakāleya. On the triplets, there are the Hārāyaṇa, Mānava, Uttarānūpa, Vāmnāgni, Triṇidhana, Vaiṣṇava, Ādyayaukta, and Sruca chants. In the *ārbhava-pavamāna*, the triplets are formed from the *uṣṇih* and *kakubh* meters. The specific distinction is that everything consists of forty-eight [verses].

For the sixth day: *Jyotir asṛkṣata* (ten verses); *Sanād divaḥ* (ten verses); *Taratsamandī* (four verses); *Eṣa kaviḥ* (six verses); *Sasutaḥ* (six verses). The *Bahiṣpavamāna* chant is performed with *Davy ete soma*. For the *Mādhyandina* and *Ārbhava* [Pavamānas], the formation of *Tṛcas* (triplets) is applied. The specific distinction is that everything consists of forty-eight verses.

On the seventh day: before the *paryāsa* hymn of the *bahiṣpavamāna*, one should place the four-verse hymn beginning with "ut te śuṣmāso asthuḥ" prior to the verse "ā te dakṣam. For both the midday and the third *pavamāna* laudations, the *tṛca* (three-verse) formation is applied. The specific rule is that everything consists of forty-eight verses. On the eighth day: before the *paryāsa* hymn, one should place the four-verse hymn beginning with "pra te dhārāḥ" prior to the verse "ayā pavasva dhārayā. For all the midday and third *pavamāna* laudations, the *tṛca* formation is applied. The specific rule is that everything consists of forty-eight verses.
The ninth day is like the twelfth day of the archetypal twelve-day sacrifice.

For the tenth day: *asṛkṣata viśvavit ajījanat ete pavasva indo dadhanvire*—this is the seven-verse [stotra]. *pra kaviḥ*—this is the seven-verse [stotra]. *yavaṃ-yavaṃ*—this is the four-verse [stotra]. *ayāvī apaghnan asya pratnān avārca*—this is the Bahiṣpavamāna. For both the Mādhyandina and Ārbhava [Pavamānas], there is the formation of all [verses] into triplets (*tṛca*). The specific distinction is that everything consists of forty-eight [verses]. ||19||
The Sixth Chapter: Variations of the Twelve-Day Sacrifice [The Tenth Day as the Avivākya]. Regarding the Avivākya-twelve-day sacrifice, he says:
Just as in the tenth [chapter].
Thus; it is to be explained as before. ||20||

He states the qualified person: "Therefore, one who desires splendor, one who desires Vedic luster, one who desires firm standing, or one who desires progeny [should perform it]; for thus the tenth day becomes dedicated to Prajāpati."

This is clear. The arrangement for this [rite] is precisely that of the first twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*). On all ten days, the *agniṣṭoma* chants must be performed with the *trayastrimśa-stoma*. The *mānasa-stotra* occurs only on the tenth day, and not on the other days.
Thus ends the fifteenth section in the third chapter.

The sixteenth section: Having described the various types of twelve-day sacrifices (*dvādaśāha*), he next states their infinity according to logical principle: "Now, therefore, the twelve-day sacrifices are infinite; for so they declare. This [topic] is concluded. 1.
He establishes its very infinity: "As many as are the Ṛg-verses and Sāman-chants, so many are the twelve-day rites, or even more than that. (2)

Thus [it is said]. Because the Sāmaveda has a thousand branches (*śākhā*), and because the *ṛcs* and *sāmans* within them are infinite, the statement "more than those" is made with reference to them. When one has studied the *sāmans* belonging to the ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*), the year-long sacrifice (*saṃvatsara*), the one-day sacrifices (*ekāha*), the multi-day sacrifices (*ahīna*), and the minor ritual systems (*kṣudratantreṣu*)—namely, the *pāvamānika* [sāmans] among the *pavamāna* chants, the *pārṣṭhika* among the *pṛṣṭha* chants, the *aukthika* among the *uktha* chants, and the *bahiṣpāvamānika* among the *bahiṣpavamāna* chants—one places a single *sāman* appropriately in the place of each individual *sāman* of the ten-night sacrifice and performs the praise (*stute*). One...

The twelve-day rite (*dvādaśāha*). Thus, by means of the *ṛc*s and *sāman*s prescribed in our own branch (*śākhā*), the infinity of the twelve-day rites is already established. Furthermore, because of the statement "and even more," the infinity of that which is already infinite is established through the inclusion of the *sāman*s found in thousands of branches as well. ||2||
Thus he describes the method for arranging an infinite number of twelve-day rites:
"One should arrange their food [in this way]: when one has mastered all the Ṛg-verses, all the Sāman-chants, and all the Stomas. (3)

Thus, "samiyāt" means "one should know. Since the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*) has already been described, the mention here of "all the *stomas*"—beginning with the *trivṛt* and so forth—is for the purpose of including everything from the *ekaviṃśa* up to the *aṣṭācatvāriṃśat* *stoma*, each individually as variations of the twelve-day sacrifice. (Chapter 6, Section 3)

Since it is impossible to arrange all the Ṛks, Sāmans, and Stomas together in one place, he explains how the arrangement of the Ṛks, Sāmans, and Stomas is to be made: "Having brought forward even a single *ṛc* from elsewhere, one should substitute it in the place of another; by that very means, that other [element] becomes the prescribed alternative. (4)

Thus; the meaning is that it occupies the place of another *ṛc*-verse belonging to the ten-night sacrifice (*daśarātra*). In this way, there is that other ritual arrangement (*kalpa*) for the *sāmans* and the *stomas*; "ritual arrangement" (*kalpa*) refers to the sacrifice (*yajña*). ||4||

He states an illustration for the point already explained: "For we see that even by means of a single *stoma*, another ritual form (*kalpa*) comes to be, as it were. For instance: 'Having made the *vāravantīya* the *agniṣṭoma-sāman* on the *revatī* verses, one desiring cattle should sacrifice. Or again, having brought a single *stoma* and substituted it in the place of another, from that very fact another ritual form comes to be. For we see that even by means of a single *stoma*, another ritual form comes to be, as it were. For instance: 'Having made the twenty-one-fold (*ekaviṃśa*) the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*, one should cause him who is afflicted with illness to sacrifice. (5)
Thus [it is said]. This is clear. ||5||

Having thus declared infinity by means of the Ṛk and Sāman verses contained in the Vedas, he now states the conceptualization of infinity according to the principle of the twelve-day rite (dvādaśāhika-rātra):

"Or rather, one should interchange the position of the two opening days (pratipad) with one another; whether it be the Stoma, the ritual arrangements (kalpa), the common framework (tantra), the Pṛṣṭha-stotras, the concluding rites (saṃsthā), or the Sāmans—by that very means, the other arrangement comes into being. (6)
Thus, since each of the *pratipad* verses and so forth corresponds to one of the twelve days, they are infinite.
For the first day, in place of the triplet beginning with "Of this ancient one" (*asya pratnām*), one should insert the verse beginning with "Flow on, foremost of speech" (*pavasva vāco 'grya*).

For the second day: in place of the *pratipad* [verse] "Pavasva vāco 'gryaḥ," one should insert the triplet beginning with "Asya pratnām. Thus, there are many variations through the transposition of the *pratipads*. For the first day: the state of having the fifteen-fold hymn-form (*pañcadaśastoma*).

The second day has the *trivṛt* as its *stoma*. Thus, due to the transposition of the *stomas*, there are many variations. The second day may take the place of the first day, and the first day may take the place of the second day; thus, there are many variations according to the different ritual arrangements (*kalpa*). On the first day, in the place of the *auśana* hymn, the final *mādhyandina* hymn of the Vasiṣṭha family, "vṛṣā śoṇa," is placed. On the second day, in the place of the Vasiṣṭha hymn, the *auśana* hymn is placed. Alternatively, on the second day, the Gāyatrī verse "uccā te" is inserted in the place of the Gāyatrī verse "vṛṣā pavasva dhārayā."

On the third day, "uccā ta" takes the place of the *gāyatra* [stotra], and "vṛṣā pavasva" [takes the place] of the [other]. In this way, through the transposition of the ritual framework (*tantra*), there are many twelve-day sacrifices (*dvādaśāha*). The first has the *bṛhat* as its *pṛṣṭha* [stotra]; the second has the *rathantara*. Thus ends the sixth chapter on the variations of the twelve-day sacrifice.

The *vāravantīya* [is used] for the sixth [day]; the *śākvara* for the sixth [day]. Thus, there are many variations due to the transposition of the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras]. However, in this case, a transposition of the *vairūpa* and *vairāja* should not be performed, because it would result in the omission of the *ṣoḍaśin*. For there is a scriptural statement: "Upon the omission of the *virāj*, the *svarāj* is omitted. Alternatively, a transposition of the *vairūpa* and *vairāja* may indeed be performed.

Because the *Nidānakāra* prescribes the *svarāja* even when there is a departure from the *virāj*, after the *yajñāyajñīya* stotra of the first day, there follow the *sākamaśva*, *mahīyava*, and *aṣṭādaṃṣṭra* *ukthas*. The second day concludes with the *agniṣṭoma* form; thus, there are many variations due to the differences in the ritual forms (*saṃsthās*). Regarding the second day: in place of the *aiḍamāyāsya*, the *porumadga* is inserted following the verse "punaḥ soma."

On the third day: in place of the *paurumadga*, the *aiḍamāyāsya* is inserted with the verse beginning "abhi soma. Thus, for domestic [animals], there are domestic *sāmans*; for wild [animals], there are wild *sāmans*. In this way, through the transposition of *sāmans*, there are many variations. Or rather, in the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*), there are many variations even through the transposition of the sequence of all the *sāmans*, such as the *āśva* and *soma-sāman*. Thus, according to the principle stated in the Sūtra, infinite twelve-day rites (*dvādaśāha*) are to be inferred; they are not written out here for fear of excessive prolixity. ||6||
By this passage it is shown that for the twelve-day rites there is only the "beyond" (apāra), not the "end" (pāra); indeed, there is no end. ||7||

Thus [it is said]. This is clear. Regarding the Agniṣṭoma, which serves as the archetype (*prakṛti*) for all sacrifices, its nature as the Vācastoma is such that because the *stomas* are infinite, its infinity has been declared. However, regarding the Dvādaśāha, it is stated: "Prajāpati indeed is this twelvefold [sacrifice], namely the twelve-night [rite]"; and "Brahman is Prajāpati"; and "The sacrifice is Prajāpati. Furthermore, according to the Taittirīya Śruti beginning with "He who is Prajāpati, being [thus], wins through the Sattra," it is said: "Prajāpati desired..."

"May I be born; may I become more. He performed austerity. Having performed austerity, he beheld this twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*). From his own limbs and from his own vital breaths (*prāṇa*), he fashioned it out of himself in twelve parts. He took it up and sacrificed with it. And elsewhere it is said: "This Prajāpati is indeed the year (*saṃvatsara*); he established himself in the seasons and in the months."

These seasons and months indeed found their support in Prajāpati, the year; they are thus established in one another. "He who sacrifices with the twelve-day rite (dvādaśāha) likewise finds support in the officiating priest," it is said. And, "This twelve-day rite is indeed the sacrifice of Prajāpati. Furthermore, "The twelve months are the year; the year is Prajāpati."

The twelve days of the *dvādaśāha* sacrifice consist of the twelve days themselves, which are the bodies (*tanvaḥ*) of Prajāpati—namely, Annādā, Annapatnī, Bhadrā, Kalyāṇī, Nilyā, Anilyā, Āptā, Anāptā, Vānāpyā, Anādhṛṣyā, Apratidhṛṣyā, and Apūrvā—and because they are composed of these twelve bodies, they possess the essential nature of Prajāpati.

Furthermore, because every sacrifice consists of twelve constituent parts—the *dīkṣaṇīyā*, *prāyaṇīyā*, *ātithyā*, three *upasads*, the *agnīṣomīya* animal sacrifice, the three pressings (*savana*), the *avabhṛtha*, the *anubandhyā*, and the *anūbandhya*—it possesses the nature of Prajāpati. As it is said: "Entering into the luminaries by means of the *śukra*, Prajāpati moves within the womb"; "Prajāpati moves within the womb; being born, he is manifested in many ways"; and "Prajāpati, the first-born of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), has by himself brought himself into existence."

"Elsewhere, he entered the Self by means of the Self. That Prajāpati alone came into being upon a lotus leaf. "In the beginning, my dear, this was Being alone, one only without a second," and "Prajāpati alone was this in the beginning. The Self is the sixth chapter—the variations of the twelve-day sacrifice.

"Or rather, in the beginning, this was indeed one alone; Brahman, indeed, was this in the beginning. Prajāpati created this Brahman, the essence of the Vedas. Having created it, he entered into that very thing" (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 6.1). And [there is the text]: "May I become many, may I procreate. Because Prajāpati is Brahman according to numerous scriptural passages, and because the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*) has that same nature, the intention of the Teachers is that it is non-different from Brahman by its very nature.

And it was said by the Blessed Āśvalāyana in the *Prayoga* of the *Dvādaśāha*: "Now, as for the general rule: because dharma is immeasurable, we shall state its specific applications (*pradeśa*). For just as a limited number of phonemes (*varṇa*) attain the status of an immeasurable range of speech, even so, from the limited number of days, there arise immeasurable combinations. However, the individual days are established; whatever collection thereof there may be, that is indeed established as praiseworthy. Thus, O Brahmin, the *Dvādaśāha* is also infinite. The *Dvādaśāha* is indeed speech (*vāk*).

This twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*) is indeed speech spread out; for Prajāpati is speech, and the sacrifice is speech, and the ritual (*kratu*) is speech. Since speech is the mouth of the sacrifice, and according to such scriptural passages as "May Prajāpati not abandon you, O Glory," it is entirely consistent that he is of the nature of glory and speech. He who has a thousand streams, who is thousandfold, who has a thousand eyes, who goes in a thousand ways, whose self is the Sāman with a thousand branches, who has a thousand rays, and who is the thousand-fold one. (1)
May the Lord of Veṅkaṭa be pleased with this thousand-fold sacrificial fee, which is embraced by the thousandfold Lakṣmī and the glory of a thousand syllables. 2.
Through the grace of the Sāmagācārya, by the favor of Tātācārya, and through the kindness of the gurus and the benevolent glance of the Brahmins. ||3||
The sixth chapter of the *Kṣudrakalpa* has been explained by the sacrificer named Śrīnivāsa, who possesses a hundredfold power and mastery of the four Vedas, for the pleasure of Hari. 4.
Thus ends the sixteenth section in the third chapter. ||16||
The third chapter is completed. ||3||

Thus ends the sixth chapter in the *Kṣudrakalpasūtrabhāṣya* composed by Śrīnivāsācārya, the performer of a hundred sacrifices (*śatakratu*) and master of the four Vedas (*caturvedi*), who was the preceptor for establishing the doctrines of the venerable Rāmānuja.
The Kṣudrakalpasūtra is completed.
